title: ‘Verity’ Thrills $4.5M Previews, ‘Digger’ Shovels $1M+ – Box Office Update
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony TIFF Midnight Madness Hit ‘River’ Gets Winter 2027 Date From Blumhouse Atomic Monster ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Worldwide Opening As Box Office Braces For ‘Digger’ Impact – Global Preview ‘Ebenezer’ Trailer: Johnny Depp Leads Ti West’s Dickens Remake View All October 2, 2026 8:32am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Verity 'and 'Digger' Amazon MGM Studios/Warner Bros. Amazon MGM Studio’s Colleen Hoover thriller Verity grossed $4.5M in its overall previews, which is right where it should for arguably the author’s second most popular novel-to-the-screen after It Ends With Us . That figure is lower than the $7M previews of the author’s mega box office hit It Ends With Us ($50M opening) and it’s ahead of the $1.9M preview cash of her Reminders of Him from earlier this year ($17.9M). Hoover’s Regretting You last fall, which Paramount released, didn’t report preview figures from 500 screens. The weekend outlook for the Dakota Johnson, Anne Hathaway, Josh Hartnett movie is $30M+. Critics have no patience for Verity, but they didn’t have patience for It Ends With Us (55% Rotten), Reminders of Him (56%) or Regretting You (29%). Watch on Deadline On a night when word leaked that Warner Bros Motion Picture Chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy weren’t making the jump to the new combined Paramount Warner Bros merger, the studio’s Tom Cruise starring, Alejandro Iñárritu directed $125M-$160M+ satire, Digger , was soft everywhere with $1.2M previews. That’s lower than the preview of last fall’s One Battle After Another ($3.1M, $22M opening). The movie will be lucky to open to north of $10M in North America. title: Jesse Jo Stark and Deadly Doll Sign With BMG
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 8:16am Jesse Jo Stark Pablo Gonzalez Jesse Jo Stark and her label Deadly Doll have signed with BMG, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Stark’s also taken on new management in Openstage co-founder Sam Jackson and Liza Owen. “Jesse Jo Stark is a distinctive artist with an unmistakable creative vision and a fearless approach to her music . We’re incredibly excited to welcome her to BMG and partner with Deadly Doll,” BMG’s Eve, Recorded Music, West Coast Dan Gill said in a statement about Stark’s signing. Gill adds, “This new album is a powerful reflection of who she is as an artist, and we look forward to helping bring it to audiences around the world.” Related Stories Music Taylor Hanson Signs With WME (Exclusive) Music Macklemore Says Free Palestine Tour "Sold Out Immediately" Last week, the singer announced her upcoming album Muse , which is set to be released on Nov. 6. The album’s first single, “Colorado,” dropped alongside the announcement. The vulnerable track also featured a music video, which was released at the same time. The upcoming album was recorded over three “snow-covered” weeks in Aspen, Colorado, and it has been described as being sonically similar to the Stark’s earlier releases. “It was the time to speak without boundary,” she said in a release about making the album. “Even though I felt broken, I also felt an immense amount of freedom. Each day felt so precious. Like I was dancing with a woman I had been hiding from. I was clear.” Deadly Doll was named after her 2017 single of the same name. It’s also the brand of the singer’s merchandise and clothing line, which has collaborated with several other high profile brands including luxury streetwear brand Chrome Hearts. The brand, which the singer serves as a VP and creative director, was co-created by her father, Richard Stark, and now run by both her father and her mother, Laurie Lynn Stark. THR

title: Mary Louise Weller, Actress in ‘Animal House,’ Dies at 79
full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 8:15am Mary Louise Weller NBCU Photo Bank/Getty Images Mary Louise Weller, who portrayed Mandy Pepperidge, the Pi House sorority sister and object of future U.S. senator John “Bluto” Blutarsky’s affection in Animal House , has died. She was 79. Weller died Thursday on the day before her birthday after a brief illness, her longtime partner Michael Roy Curtis announced. A former Ford model and longtime spokesperson for Jean Naté fragrance, Weller also played a Southern guest editor at a New York fashion magazine in the Larry Peerce-directed adaptation of Sylvia Plath’s The Bell Jar (1979) and was the love interest of Chuck Norris ’ character in the Hong Kong-set Forced Vengeance (1982). Related Stories Business Martin A. Grove, Longtime Columnist for The Hollywood Reporter, Dies at 83 TV Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio, the Italian Puppet on 'The Ed Sullivan Show,' Dies at 100 Weller also showed up on such TV shows as Baretta , Kojak , Starsky & Hutch , Supertrain , Vegas , Fantasy Island , CHiPs and, for her final onscreen credit, a 1983 episode of Quincy, M.E. During her brief acting career, “I was the beautiful girl in trouble or the rich guy’s daughter who owns a Porsche and won’t give you the time of day,” she noted in a 1986 interview with the Los Angeles Times . In the box office sensation Animal House (1978), directed by John Landis, Weller sparkled as the snooty Mandy, who’s dating the arrogant Omega House chapter president Gregory Marmalard (James Daughton). Mary Louise Weller with James Daughton in ‘Animal House.’ Courtesy Everett Collection In one scene, John Belushi ’s Bluto of Delta House climbs a ladder to watch Mandy slowly disrobe in her bedroom, and in the film’s “Where are they now?” epilogue , it’s revealed that the two will marry and live in Washington, D.C., with Blutarsky in the Senate. An only child, Weller was born in New York on Oct. 2, 1946, and raised in Westwood since she was about 10. Famed actor Danny Kaye was her godfather; he was a friend of her father, Alex, a doctor. Her mother, Annette, was a homemaker. In one of her first acting jobs, she appeared uncredited in a party scene in Sidney Lumet’s Serpico (1973), starring Al Pacino. The year 1978 was a big one for her. In addition to Animal House , she portrayed a marine biologist in the NBC telefilm Hunters of the Reef and a college student opposite Andrew Prine in the horror movie The Evil . Weller later had a small role in the supernatural fantasy Q (1982), written and directed by Larry Cohen . Weller acted onstage in New York; wrote a play, Four Alone , that was performed at the Greenhouse Theater in Pasadena with a grant from the National Endowment for the Arts; and sought to produce a film based on the life of jockey Mary Bacon before leaving show business. (Weller had trained with the U.S. Equestrian team as a teenager and loved horses; Curtis designs courses for equestrian events.) Survivors include her cousin Sheila Weller, an author who wrote books including the 2003 family memoir Dancing at Ciro’s: A Family’s Love, Loss, and Scandal on the Sunset Strip and 2008’s Girls Like Us: Carole King, Joni Mitchell, Carly Simon — and the Journey of a Generation. Asked in 2012 if she knew Animal House would be a success, Weller replied she “was pretty sure” and added: “I remember showing [the script] to Brandon Stoddard, who was head of ABC at that time. He also knew it would be an enormous hit … but he warned me that it would be the movie I would always be known for.” THR

title: Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest AGC Studios Launches AGC Digital, a Division Focused on Nurturing Creator-Led Intellectual Property 1 day ago Thessaloniki’s Agora Crossroads Co-production Forum to Feature 14 Projects From 15 Countries 1 day ago Woody Allen’s New Movie to Star Marton Csokas, Jemima Kirke and More as WestEnd Boards Sales 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Music Box Films Music Box Films has acquired North American rights for documentary “ Steal This Story, Please! ,” and will release the film on all major digital platforms on Oct 20. The film, initially self-distributed by the filmmakers, had a successful theatrical release across the U.S. in the spring, grossing close to $1 million. “Steal This Story, Please!,” which focuses on the work of trailblazing independent journalist Amy Goodman , is directed by Academy Award nominees Carl Deal and Tia Lessin. Popular on Variety Related Stories Alan Cumming Sheds His 'Traitors' Kilt for 'Tip Toe', a Searing Parable of Homophobic Backlash: TV Review Music Box will also release the film on DVD and Blu-ray with the physical media release date to be announced. It will have a live online screening on Oct. 13 at 8 p.m. ET, followed by a live Q&A talkback with Goodman, alongside Lessin and Deal (“Trouble the Water,” “Citizen Koch,” “The Janes”). Premiering at the 2025 Telluride Film Festival, “Steal This Story, Please!” went on to win audience awards at 11 festivals — including Mill Valley, Palm Springs, Santa Barbara and Woodstock. The film, which had theatrical booking support from Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media, opened on a single screen in New York at the IFC Center in April, grossed over $30,000 opening weekend and was held over for 12 weeks. Expanding nationally, the documentary screened in more than 50 markets and was one of the best performing non-fiction releases of this year. Music Box has acquired the film for theatrical and home entertainment rights, taking over theatrical bookings moving forward. In a statement, the distributor said that Goodman “has reported some of the most urgent and underreported stories of our time on her daily global newshour Democracy Now!. Drawing on an extraordinary archive, filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin take us behind the scenes with the warm, wisecracking granddaughter of an Orthodox rabbi — raised in a tradition of asking hard questions — as she navigates a media landscape reshaped by technology, corporate consolidation, and political assaults on the press.” It added, “Urgent, provocative and unexpectedly funny, ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ explores what’s at stake when journalism is threatened, and why the act of bearing witness has never mattered more.” Deal said, “We are thrilled that ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ will be part of the Music Box family of high-quality independent films, and that Amy’s story will get to home audiences far and wide at a moment when free expression is in the crosshairs of the President of the United States.” Lessin added, “Long before attacks on the press became a defining feature of our political life, Amy Goodman understood that democracy depends on independent, uncompromised journalism that doesn’t bow to power. We are excited to join forces with Music Box Films to build on the theatrical success of the film and ensure that it reaches home audiences in the same spirit of editorial freedom and direct engagement that has defined Amy’s work, as well as our own.” “ ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ had the highest-grossing week of any documentary in the history of the Music Box Theatre in Chicago,” said Music Box Films. “We are thrilled to continue our relationship with Amy, Carl and Tia, in expanding the audience reach of this powerful documentary.” “In a marketplace where industry leaders continually harp on about the limited theatrical prospects for documentaries – especially those of a political nature – the unabashed success of ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ proves that audiences are still wanting to be moved and entertained,” said Tuckman. “Grossing close to a million, the release is a testament to Carl and Tia’s belief that theaters are still the best place for documentaries to engage and inspire audiences.” “Steal This Story, Please!” is executive produced by Jane Fonda, Rosario Dawson, Tom Morello, Sheila Nevins, Julie Cohen, Tony Tabatznik, Bill Haney, Jonathan Logan and Steve Silberstein, produced by Deal and Lessin, with producers Karen Ranucci, Diana Cohn and Caren Spruch. The sale of the home entertainment rights was negotiated by Brian Andreotti on behalf of Music Box Films and Ben Schwartz and Joe Tufano at Submarine. title: How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’
full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’ By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Nathan Fielder Speaks Out on Living With Elizabeth Holmes While Filming ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: ‘She Seems So Genuine’ but ‘I Know She’s a Liar’ 1 day ago Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Found Guilty of Murdering Wife 3 days ago Elizabeth Holmes Posts Cryptic Message From Prison Ahead of ‘You Can See Everything’ Release: ‘I Was Silenced for a Long Time’ 4 days ago See All Courtesy of A24 Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim shocked Hollywood and the world when they revealed they’d secretly been filming Elizabeth Holmes ahead of her 11-year prison sentence for their documentary, “ You Can See Everything .” The film had a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival last month and had another early screening at the New York Film Festival on Wednesday, where the co-directors peeled the curtain back on how they pulled off the shoot. Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invited Fielder, Oppenheim and a small camera crew into their San Diego home 34 days before Holmes began her Theranos fraud prison sentence. Fielder, who makes his feature directorial debut with the film, is known for blending bizarre, real subjects with absurd, scripted comedy on his shows “Nathan for You” and “The Rehearsal.” But he had planned to stay behind the camera when he and Oppenheim embarked on “You Can See Everything.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Paranormal Comedy 'Don't F — k With Ghosts' Premieres On Demand, Launches Original YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale “I was like, ‘I’m definitely not going to be in this when we started,’” Fielder said. “I was behind the camera with Lance, and it was strange. [Holmes and Evans] would keep talking to me or asking me questions, and I would answer from off-camera. But then eventually, the operators would start panning over to me because the conversations would be long.” “You became this accidental investigator of everyday moments,” Oppenheim added. “I feel like that also came about too because the way we were shooting it initially was with one camera and anamorphic lenses, and it was extremely cumbersome. It was the wrong approach for this. Every time we would miss a moment or try to change a lens, that would be when they would also be engaging Nathan off-camera. So eventually, probably about a day of getting it fully wrong, we decided essentially to completely change the way both of us work.” Fielder and Oppenheim both brought crew members from their past projects, including cinematographer David Bolen, who worked on Oppenheim’s recent film “Primetime” and his docs “Spermworld” and “Some Kind of Heaven.” “It basically made us work in this completely new way, which oddly and ironically, is as close to the tenets of documentary filming, which is just fly-on-the-wall, vérité filmmaking,” Oppenheim said. “So we had three cameras, two operators, one would be sometimes on Elizabeth or Billy, one would be on Nathan, and we basically pick zones of the house and have these extremely long zoom lenses. Then I would be hidden behind the wide camera. We were trying to do that in an effort to try and take all the pressure away from any moment. We would be shooting like 16 hours a day, so they wouldn’t really know what we were interested in necessarily.” “We didn’t always know either,” Fielder joked. “We started setting up the cameras where we had a wide lens that would cover the whole house, so if something happened, we wouldn’t miss it. The other two 25mm to 250mm lenses could be wide, but then also zoom, so we could basically capture everything.” Fielder revealed that the crew was comprised of just seven people, and only four of them would be inside Holmes’ house at any time. He also shouted out Bolen, who “found a way to make shots look beautiful in the day or the night.” “As long as there was a light, we could make it work,” Fielder said. “If we were live and then something interesting started happening, [Bolen] could pick up the camera and tripod, move to a new spot, re-lock the head in 10 seconds. It looks amazing, and it’s a testament to the team who put this together. It was down to this whole dance we had, and it was just amazing and one of the best experiences I think we’ve had making something because of that exploratory freedom and being able to let our curiosity drive us.” Oppenheim and Bolen collaborated on “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen. The film was shot in a boxy 4:3 aspect ratio to mimic the retro, reality TV look of “To Catch a Predator” from the 2000s. Oppenheim used the same format on “You Can See Everything” to get close-up, reaction shots from Holmes, Evans and Fielder. “One thing we realized with the one camera that’s panning is that the moment you say something to someone, you want to see their face the moment they hear it,” Fielder said. “Especially in a movie like this, where you’re trying to evaluate if someone’s being honest or not, when you have to swing, you’re missing a few seconds.” Oppenheim added, “The aspect ratio of the movie came about because we’re confined largely in one space, and there was so much. Every time we put the camera somewhere, when we originally were in a larger aspect ratio, it felt like you were seeing so many details that were distracting you from the human face. The face is the ultimate landscape. You wanted to be on their faces when something would happen and really study it and linger there, because that could get the closest you could possibly be to being there.” Taylor Swift Announces ‘The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore’ Album With Four New Songs Taylor Swift Praises Phoebe Bridgers’ New Album ‘Lost Weekend,’ Calls It an ‘Absolute Triumph in Every Way’ Dakota Johnson on Being in Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video: ‘We Respect Each Other’s Creative Minds’ Taylor Swift Recalls How ‘I Knew You Were Trouble’ Was Written as a ‘Really Sad Ballad’ in Grammy Museum Conversation Video Todd Rundgren Slams Taylor Swift, Says She ‘Ruined Music’ and Is ‘the Apotheosis of Mediocrity’ Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in ‘SVU’ Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise Loading comments...

full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:02am PT Disney Licenses Slew of Titles to Netflix, Including All Five ‘Ice Age’ Movies, ‘Percy Jackson and the Olympians,’ ‘Felicity,’ ‘Will Trent,’ ‘Elio’ and More (EXCLUSIVE) By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest New Name of Paramount-Warner Bros. Disney Entertainment and Netflix have entered into an expansive new content licensing agreement, which will bring an eclectic mix of library titles and current-season TV shows to Netflix for varying periods of times on a nonexclusive basis. Related Stories Emmys in Talks to Move to Amazon Prime Video Under New Licensing Arrangement, as the Broadcast Wheel Deal Ends (EXCLUSIVE) Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale In some cases, part of Disney’s strategy is to drum up interest in upcoming releases. Disney+ original series “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” Seasons 1-2 will be available on Netflix globally beginning Oct. 4 as part of a three-month promotional window in advance of its Season 3 premiere on Disney+ on Nov. 20. Popular on Variety Similarly, all five of 20th Century Studios’ “Ice Age” films will be available on Netflix worldwide beginning Oct. 4 in a separate three-month promotional window ahead of the franchise’s sixth installment, “Ice Age: Boiling Point,” releasing in theaters on Feb. 5, 2027. The movies are “Ice Age” (2002), “Ice Age: The Meltdown” (2006), “Ice Age: Dawn of the Dinosaurs” (2009), “Ice Age: Continental Drift” (2012) and “Ice Age: Collision Course” (2016). Three current series from 20th Television also are coming to Netflix: Crime drama “Will Trent” Seasons 1-4 and sitcom “Shifting Gears” Seasons 1-2 will be available on Netflix globally, while action-drama “Tracker” Seasons 1-3 will be available on Netflix internationally outside the U.S. as part of a multiyear term. “Will Trent” (S1-4) will be on Netflix globally as of Nov. 3, ahead of the Season 5 premiere on ABC in early 2027. “Shifting Gears” (S1-2) is coming to Netflix beginning Dec. 1 in the U.S. and internationally in January, ahead of the Season 3 premiere on ABC on Jan. 7, 2027. “Tracker” (S1-3) will be available on Netflix internationally as of Feb. 26, 2027; Season 4 premieres on CBS on Oct. 4. The deal includes a selection of non-franchised Disney-branded films from Walt Disney Animation Studios and Pixar. Beginning in early 2027, Oscar-winner “Soul,” “Elio,” “Raya and the Last Dragon” and other movies will be will be available to stream on Netflix globally (with title availability and launch dates varying by region). In addition, a selection of library series from Disney Entertainment will be available on Netflix. Those include “Felicity” (available on Netflix in the U.S. Oct. 7, internationally at later dates), “Revenge” (global), “Army Wives” (global), “Fresh Off the Boat” (U.S. and select regions) and “This Is Us” (internationally outside the U.S.; it had been previously licensed to Netflix in 2024-25 in the U.S.). The new batch of Disney-owned TV shows and movies will join other licensed content from the media conglomerate on Netflix, including “Grey’s Anatomy,” “Arrested Development,” “Scandal” and “Black-ish.” From Disney’s perspective, the expanded licensing pact is a win-win: Disney is bringing the collection of titles to a broader audience to boost their visibility (while also generating millions in incremental revenue) and Netflix is adding more content offerings. And Disney is not deviating from its general strategy in which Disney-branded titles remain largely exclusive to its platforms and TV channels. All titles that are currently on Disney+ (including the “Ice Age” movies and “Percy Jackson”) and Hulu will continue to be available. Netflix, in addition to a broad lineup of licensed titles, also spends a bunch of money on originals. Those include animated hit films “KPop Demon Hunters” and “Swapped.” Its upcoming slate of originals includes “Steps” (Nov. 20), “Charlie vs. the Chocolate Factory” and Guillermo del Toro’s “The Buried Giant,” with sequels to “Leo” and “KPop Demon Hunters” in the works. title: Music Industry Moves: Frank Briegmann Gets a Big Up at Universal Music; Warner Mexico Promotes Yusim Aladro to GM
full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:00am PT Music Industry Moves: Frank Briegmann Gets a Big Up at Universal Music; Warner Mexico Promotes Yusim Aladro to GM By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Venom Frontman Conrad ‘Cronos’ Lant Dies at 63 17 hours ago Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’ 23 hours ago Sia Sells 50% of Music Catalog to Pophouse in $180 Million Partnership Deal 1 day ago See All Universal Music Group has promoted Frank Briegmann to Chairman & CEO, Universal Music Europe, Australia, New Zealand, Canada & Deutsche Grammophon. He will continue to report to Lucian Grainge, Chairman & CEO of Universal Music Group. Briegmann will work closely with the leadership in each market, including Olivier Nusse who continues as CEO, Universal Music France; Sean Warner who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Australia & New Zealand; and Julie Adam who continues as President & CEO, Universal Music Canada. Spain will continue to be led by Luis Fernández, President, Universal Music Spain, and Portugal will continue to be led by Ana Hernandez, Managing Director, Portugal, both reporting to Jesus Lopez. The United Kingdom will continue to be led by Dickon Stainer, Chairman & CEO, U.K., reporting to Grainge. Related Stories Alan Cumming Sheds His 'Traitors' Kilt for 'Tip Toe', a Searing Parable of Homophobic Backlash: TV Review Briegmann joined Universal Music in 2004 as CEO of its German business, becoming the youngest executive ever to lead a major music company in Germany. His responsibilities have since expanded across Central, Northern and Eastern Europe, alongside his global leadership of Deutsche Grammophon. Popular on Variety “Frank and I have worked together for more than 20 years, and he’s a fierce artist champion with a proven track record of building long-term careers, Grainge said. “He combines creative expertise with business acumen and the insights of data and technology. Just as importantly, he respects what makes every market different and knows how to give great local leaders the freedom and support to succeed. Frank’s promotion is all about the power of possibility; making it easier for artists, ideas, and opportunities to travel across borders.” + Warner Music Mexico has promoted Yusim Aladro to the role of General Manager. Aladro, who joined the company at the start of the year, reports to Tomas Rodriguez, President of Warner Music Mexico. According to the announcement, Aladro will spearhead the strategic direction and development of all domestic music within the country, and “drive seamless integration across A&R, creative marketing, and artists’ brand building to accelerate cross-border success for Mexican artists globally, while continuing to expand relationships within the artist, management, and independent label community.” She was previously Director of Marketing and has worked closely with Myke Towers, Elena Rose, Flvckka and Yng Lvcas. Previously, she held senior leadership positions at Rico o Muerto, Downtown Artist & Label Services, Altafonte, Auditorio Nacional México, and Alive Entertainment. “Yusim represents the modern, holistic music executive – combining a deep, intuitive understanding of artist development and creative strategy with sharp commercial acumen,” Rodriguez said. “Her leadership will not only accelerate the growth of our domestic roster but also inspire the next generation of women leaders across the Latin music industry.” + King, Holmes, Paterno & Soriano has promoted Erika Savage to partner. At the firm, Savage represents artists, songwriters, managers and independent music companies across recorded music, live performance, influencer marketing, endorsement agreements and other areas. Her clients have included Pink, Dr. Dre, Tyler, The Creator, Blink-182, Carole King, Sia and Melanie Martinez, as well as independent labels and music companies including Sub Pop, Ghetto Youths International, The Core, Nice Life Records and Victor Victor Worldwide. Before joining the firm, Erika served as SVP of Global Music Operations at United Talent Agency, overseeing operations for its global touring division including leading its Business Affairs team and handling strategic planning. Prior to UTA, Erika spent 19 years at Universal Music Group, including as SVP Strategic Development at Interscope Records, where she led Interscope’s non-record revenue business and developed artist strategies across music, brand partnerships, merchandise and touring. She also negotiated recording agreements and handled Business Affairs matters for a roster that included Lady Gaga, Lana Del Rey and Billie Eilish. Managing Partner Howard King commented: “We are delighted to acknowledge Erika’s hard work and strategic vision in helping the firm provide superb service to our clients.” + Plot Twist Records , the independent record label founded by veteran A&R Executive and media personality Carter Gregory, has formed a joint venture deal with 10K Projects and Atlantic Records . The first signings to the label include singer Alabama Barker and DJ/artist Nic Vans (Nic Vansteenberghe), who gained prominence as the runner-up contestant on the reality TV series “Love Island USA.” The joint venture follows Plot Twist’s independent launch, during which Gregory signed and released Kylie Jenner’s debut single, “Fourth Strike.” Most recently, Gregory served as a VP of A&R at Capitol Records, where he worked closely with such artists as Fletcher, Doechii, Adela, Queen Naija and others. He is also the host of the podcast “The Set List.” “Carter is not only an expert at identifying culturally impactful artists who are moving the needle, but he’s exceptionally talented in creating communities around the music he loves,” said Atlantic Music Group COO Zach Friedman. “We’re thrilled to be working closely with him on his expanding roster of artists at Plot Twist.” + Artist-songwriter-producer Taylor Hanson has signed with WME for worldwide representation in all areas. He was recently a contestant on Season 35 of “Dancing with the Stars” on ABC. The Oklahoma and Los Angeles-based musician is also working on his debut solo album, planned for release in 2027. Hanson rose to fame in 1997 when Hanson, the band he formed with his brothers Isaac and Zac, released their major label debut, “Middle of Nowhere,” featuring the global hit single “MMMBop.” Over the years the group has earned three Grammy nominations. Hanson was also part of the group Tinted Windows with Bun E Carlos (Cheap Trick), James Iha (Smashing Pumpkins) and the late Adam Schlesinger (Fountains of Wayne). + Warner Music Central Europe has announced the appointment of Nici Ochmann as its Head of Culture & Creator Marketing, effective immediately. In the newly created role, Ochmann will shape the company’s culture and creator marketing strategy in GSA by developing artist and creator-led partnerships and campaigns, authentic cross-industry collaborations, and digital-first cultural narratives; she will also build partnerships with domestic and international artists and creators who are in GSA. She is based in the company’s Berlin headquarters. Ochmann moves to WM Central Europe following a 10-year tenure at Adidas, where she most recently served as Global Culture Marketing Cluster Lead for GSA. Niels Walboomers, President of Warner Music Central Europe, says, “Nici brings an invaluable perspective from the lifestyle space, where its culture moves at lightning speed. Her ability to bridge brand narrative with creator dynamics makes her the perfect fit for our vision of the company and will play a vital role in ensuring our artists stay at the bleeding edge of fan connection.” SoundExchange has announced the appointment of Paul Shaver as Senior Vice President, Business Development. He will report to President and Chief Executive Officer Michael Huppe. Shaver joins SoundExchange from the Canadian Musical Reproduction Rights Agency, where he served as President of both CMRRA and SX Works. In his new role, Shaver will spearhead SoundExchange’s efforts to identify strategic growth opportunities, develop innovative partnerships, and expand the organization’s impact across the music ecosystem. He will also help shape SoundExchange’s approach to emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, as the organization evolves to meet the future needs of creators and rights owners. Prior to CMRRA, Shaver held senior leadership positions with Nielsen Entertainment, Universal Music Group, EMI/Capitol Music, and Virgin Records. + “Paul is a respected and forward-thinking executive with experience across many aspects of the music industry,” said Huppe. “He has a proven ability to anticipate change, build innovative solutions, and turn opportunity into growth. As technology reshapes how music is created, distributed, and monetized, Paul’s leadership will help SoundExchange expand its impact and remain at the forefront of the industry’s evolution.” Tuesday, Sept. 29 Universal Music Group has named Libby Bush to the newly created role of President, Global Brands and Commercial Partnerships, starting in November. According to the announcement, she will “lead a new global function that brings together UMG’s brands, media, and commercial partnership businesses, including Universal Music Group for Brands … Spanning digital platforms, physical products and live experiences, these collaborations will be rooted in artists’ originality and authentic connections with fans.” Based in Los Angeles, Bush will report to UMG’s Chief Operating Officer Boyd Muir. She joins from Creative Artists Agency, where she served as Global Head of Entertainment Partnerships and was a member of the Agency Board. Previously, Bush founded Tandem Entertainment, an entertainment partnerships agency acquired by CAA in 2020, and held roles at Marvel Entertainment, ABC Entertainment, the WNBA’s Los Angeles Sparks and the National Basketball Association. Muir said, “As the ways fans experience music evolve, the opportunities for our artists multiply. Bringing our brand, media, and commercial partnerships together under Libby’s leadership will help extend our artists’ reach and grow their revenues, while giving our partners new ways to build relationships with fans and collaborate with the world’s most influential voices. Libby brings exceptional creative and commercial expertise to the world’s leading music company. She’ll work with our talent, teams, and partners to create memorable experiences for fans, lasting value for brands, and new possibilities for artists.” + Avex Inc. has increased its ownership of Brandon Silverstein’s S10 Entertainment , acquiring 85% of the company from Silverstein and his partners. The transaction further integrates S10 into Avex Music Group. Silverstein continues as CEO of S10 and Avex Music Group, a board member and equity partner in Avex Music Group. Terms of the deal were not disclosed. The transaction follows Avex’s March 2025 acquisition of the S10 Music Publishing catalog, which includes shares of hits by Justin Bieber, Drake, Tate McRae, Kehlani, Doja Cat, Post Malone and Rihanna, among others. In the transaction Silverstein was represented by Skadden, Arps, Slate, Meagher & Flom LLP. “S10 is an exceptional management company that is playing a key role in realizing our global ambitions,” said Katsumi Kuroiwa, CEO of Avex Inc. “Bringing S10 into Avex reflects our confidence in Brandon’s leadership and our commitment to growing Avex’s global music business. Together, we will bring the full breadth of Avex’s capabilities to artists and creators around the world.” + Warner Music Group has named Sonny Takhar as Chairman and CEO of Warner Music U.K. & Ireland, effective January 2027. Takhar will oversee creative direction, artist development, and strategic operations across WMG’s recorded music footprint in the U.K., the world’s third-largest music market, and Ireland. Takhar will report to Val Blavatnik, Managing Director of Warner Music North America, U.K. & Corporate Development. Takhar’s remit will also include operational oversight of WMG’s independent distribution arm, ADA, in the U.K. and Ireland, and he’ll work in close partnership with Elliot Grainge, CEO and Chairman of Atlantic Music Group and Chairman of ADA in the U.S., as well as Aaron Bay-Schuck, Chairman and CEO of Warner Records Group. A founding partner of Syco Entertainment, Takhar played a key role in the careers of One Direction, Labrinth, Leona Lewis, Little Mix, James Arthur and Fifth Harmony, alongside the launch of global TV franchises “The X Factor” and “Got Talent.” More recently, Takhar co-founded Los Angeles-based KYN Entertainment in a joint venture with Live Nation, and worked with Westlife and songwriter-producer Steve Mac. Blavatnik said, “Sonny is one of the most visionary executives in music and his track record of discovering, nurturing, and breaking global superstars speaks for itself. His instinct for talent, deep understanding of the wider music ecosystem and strategic global perspective make him the perfect leader to power Warner Music UK & Ireland forward.” + Amra , the global digital collection society, today announced that its Chief Executive Officer, Tomas Ericsson , will transition from his role as CEO after 13 years, effective January 1, 2027. He will assume the role of Chairman of the Board. Robin Davies , Amra’s Chief Operating Officer for the last four years, has been named Chief Executive Officer of the company beginning on January 1st. Ericsson launched Amra in partnership with Kobalt Music Group in 2013, ultimately licensing digital rights directly across more than 200 territories, 45 publishers and growing into nine figures gross by 2026. “We are so grateful for Tomas’ vision and leadership as he and his team have built amra into one of the industry’s most innovative and transformational organizations,” said Laurent Hubert, CEO of Kobalt. “We are also looking forward to Tomas continuing to contribute to the business as Chairman. amra will be in good hands with Tomas’ ongoing guidance and with Robin, who has been with amra and the Kobalt organization for a decade, at the helm.” + Danny Goldberg has promoted Jesse Bauer to the position of Senior Vice-President and Gabriel Barreto to Vice President of Gold Village Entertainment, the New York based artist management company that Goldberg launched in 2007. Bauer has been with the company since its inception; Barreto joined in 2021. Gold Village represents Steve Earle, the Waterboys, and others. + Music Services , a division of SESAC Music Group, has named Nick LaPointe Senior Director of Business Development, and Jay Sudarma Vice President of Marketing for Music Services and CCLI Group. LaPointe joins from FUGA AVS and previously held roles at AdRev and Warner Chappell Music; Sudarm’s new role comes alongside a promotion to Vice President of Marketing at CCLI Group, where he previously served as Director of Marketing. Both appointments are effective immediately. “We’re thrilled to welcome Nick to the team. Throughout his career, he has earned the trust of independent publishers and labels by helping them turn their rights into meaningful revenue,” said Rose Cook, Chief Operating Officer, Music Services. “During his tenure at CCLI, Jay has proven the value of a disciplined, data-driven approach to marketing, and this expanded role is a natural next step,” said Cook. “He will work across brands in the Music Services portfolio, including AudioSalad, Audiam, Music Services Inc., The Harry Fox Agency, HAAWK, and CCLI, bringing a unified voice to a growing collection of brands while preserving the qualities that make each one unique.” + ASCAP President and Chairman of the Board Paul Williams has announced that Jim Selby has been elected as a publisher member to the ASCAP Board of Directors. Jim Selby is President, Global Music Publishing at BMG, leading the company’s worldwide music publishing, and played a key role in its recent merger with Concord. Williams commented: “The ASCAP Board cares deeply about making decisions that are in the best interests of the membership as a whole. As a global publishing leader, Jim has the expertise to tackle the complex issues facing music creators and publishers in today’s market, from both the challenges and opportunities of AI to licensees who want to pay songwriters less. He will be an invaluable voice on the ASCAP Board in our mission to advocate for and protect our more than one million members.” + Universal Music Group has named Òscar Celma as Senior Vice President, Applied AI and Machine Learning, effective immediately. Celma will help lead the development and application of AI and machine learning across UMG’s global operations, supporting UMG’s labels, divisions and businesses. He will report to Hannah Poferl, UMG’s Chief Data Officer. In his previous role at Spotify, Celma helped lead the development of AI-powered personalized listening experiences including AI DJ, Jam and Daylist, as well as personalization and discovery. He also held roles at Conde Nast, Pandora/SiriusXM and BMAT Music Innovators. Poferl said, “Òscar brings a unique blend of quantitative and product experience, deep expertise in AI, and a love of music. He’s built teams that have delivered and knows how to turn data at scale into useful insights. With the breadth and depth of UMG’s data, there’s enormous potential for him to help our teams do more for our artists.” + Chrysalis Records , part of the Reservoir group of companies, and associated artist management & music publishing company Blue Raincoat Music announced that broadcaster-journalist Steve Lamacq has joined the company as Curator, New Music & Talent Development. The newly created consultancy role focused on helping both companies identify, champion and nurture the next generation of breakthrough artists. Working alongside Chrysalis’ and Blue Raincoat’s existing A&R, management and creative teams in a consultancy capacity, Lamacq, a veteran of the BBC and NME, will help discover, champion and develop emerging talent, drawing on more than four decades of experience at the forefront of alternative and independent music culture. Lamacq was appointed an MBE in 2025 for services to broadcasting and to music venues. Jeremy Lascelles, CEO of Chrysalis Records & Blue Raincoat Music said: “Steve has an extraordinary ability to spot great artists early. Time and again he’s identified talent long before the wider industry catches on. When I asked him if he fancied working alongside us in this capacity, I was over the proverbial moon when he agreed. It’s pretty much a dream scenario for us. Alongside his deep knowledge of music, he has built a level of trust with artists and audiences alike, that makes him uniquely qualified for this curating role. title: ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival Cast, Whitney Leavitt, Mason Alexander Park Among Variety’s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for 2026
full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:00am PT ‘Spring Awakening’ Revival Cast, Whitney Leavitt, Mason Alexander Park Among Variety’s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for 2026 By Haley Kluge , Rebecca Rubin Variety is proud to announce the 2026 edition of its annual 10 Broadway Stars to Watch. These actors, composers, librettists, and playwrights — working on shows including “Purple Rain,” “Warriors,” “Spring Awakening,” “10 Things I Hate About You” and “Wanted” — represent the future of theater. This year’s roster of standouts will be honored at our annual Business of Broadway Breakfast, hosted by Tom Felton, who is currently reprising his signature role, Draco Malfoy, in the play “Harry Potter and the Cursed Child.” At the Oct. 5 event, Variety will celebrate the upcoming season with exclusive conversations with Rachel Zegler, Diego Rodriguez and James Olivas for “Evita,” which opens in spring 2027; Aaron Sorkin, Bradley Whitford, Tom Blyth, Krysta Rodriguez and Michael Arden for “A Few Good Men,” which begins previews on Oct. 8; and Bartlett Sher, Adam Speers and the cast of “Dolly: A True Original Musical,” which launches in January 2027. Here are Variety ‘s 10 Broadway Stars to Watch for the 2026-27 season. Jethro Compton, ‘The Curious Case of Benjamin Button’ Compton likes wearing many hats. After writing the book and lyrics for “The Curious Case of Benjamin Button,” designing the set and directing the show on the West End, he’s bringing it all stateside. The musical — which retains only the core premise of F. Scott Fitzgerald’s short story and departs significantly from the David Fincher film — sets the tale in a Cornish fishing village, with a folk score performed by a cast of actor-musicians as Benjamin ages backwards. Compton’s urge to multitask came out of necessity. He started as a producer working with “exceptionally tight margins.” “I realized the only way I could make the budgets stack up was to hire myself to do as many roles as possible. It also turned out to be a wonderfully efficient way of working, as it drastically reduced the number of meetings I had to attend,” he says. His resourcefulness is clearly working — Compton has been developing the show for seven years, and its West End iteration brought home three Olivier Awards, including for best new musical. “For me, writing and directing are completely different skill sets that require very different ways of thinking. I don’t feel like I’m ever wearing both hats at the same time,” he says. “In the writing room, I’m a writer. In the rehearsal room, I’m the director.” He adds, “I love and loathe them in equal measure!” First West End show “Les Misérables” Most listened to cast album “Come From Away” Theater superstition you believe “It’s bad luck to say, “Good luck,’ on opening night.” Peter Duchan, ‘Purple Rain’ and ‘Practical Magic’ Years ago, Duchan was warned not to expect success as a librettist until he was in his 40s: “I’ve always understood this career as something of an endurance test.” At 43, he’s making his Broadway debut with “Purple Rain,” the stage version of the classic Prince album and film, about the rise of a tormented young musician known as the Kid. Duchan’s big break comes more than a decade after he emerged on the New York theater scene with 2012’s Off Broadway musical “Dogfight,” based on the 1991 movie starring River Phoenix. “We’re trying to honor what’s singular about Prince while crafting a fictional character separate from him,” Duchan says. An adept multitasker (and an expert at translating from screen to stage), Duchan is working on another major musical adaptation, “Practical Magic,” based on the 1998 fantasy comedy starring Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock as witchy sisters. “These are just the two you know about!” Duchan teases. “I spend all day, every day, thinking about musical-theater storytelling. If I haven’t clocked my 10,000 hours yet, I’ve gotta be pretty close.” First Broadway show “Les Misérables” at the Broadway Theatre Go-to Broadway karaoke song “The Feeling We Once Had” from “The Wiz” Show that needs a revival “We haven’t seen ‘The Most Happy Fella’ on Broadway in over 30 years.” Aneesa Folds, ‘Warriors’ It’s hard to typecast Folds. The actress, comedian, writer and improviser has built a career at the intersection of musical theater, hip-hop and comedy. As a high schooler, Folds posted on Tumblr that Freestyle Love Supreme was “everything I’ve ever wanted to do.” Years later, in 2019, she made her Broadway debut with the act. “Freestyle Love Supreme is the thing that taught me that you as yourself is enough,” she says. “You can just be who you are.” Since then, she’s created and performed her own work and starred as Hallie Parker in the “Parent Trap” spoof “Ginger Twinsies.” “I get to do such strange things, and I love it,” she says. “My last thing was playing an 11-year-old white girl.” Now she’s reuniting with frequent collaborator Lin-Manuel Miranda on “Warriors,” his concept album with Eisa Davis that’s headed to Broadway in spring 2027. The musical reimagines the cult film’s gang as women. And for Folds, a Queens native with “music in my blood,” it’s also a celebration of her hometown. “It’s every single genre in the world of New York,” she says. “For anyone seeing it, listening to it, you’re going to relate to something, no matter what.” She adds, “It’s not about fragile, delicate women. It’s about women fighting and standing up for themselves.” As for what’s next? “Theater is in a weird place right now. Let’s just fuck it up.” First Broadway show “The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee” Show that needs a revival “Seussical” Ethan Gruska and Carly Rae Jepsen, ’10 Things I Hate About You’ Image Credit: Courtesy Images More than a decade after Jepsen made her Broadway debut in the 2014 revival of “Rodgers + Hammerstein’s Cinderella,” she’s returning to the New York stage — this time as a songwriter. She and Gruska are composing the music for “10 Things I Hate About You,” a musical by Lena Dunham and Jessica Huang that’s based on the classic 1999 teen rom-com. Jepsen is best known as the Grammy-nominated singer of “Call Me Maybe” and “I Really Like You,” while Gruska is a producer who has worked with Phoebe Bridgers, Fiona Apple, and Bon Iver. They first collaborated on Jepsen’s 2023 album “The Loveliest Time,” and Gruska describes having “immediate chemistry.” For Jepsen, crafting tunes for Broadway requires a “different side of the brain” than writing pop songs. “I find it so challenging in the best way,” she says. “We get to play with humor and all these deep emotions, which is so satisfying.” Knowing how much people love the movie, the duo is striving to handle the material “with care but not trepidation.” With a year until the musical begins previews, Jepsen says, “I’m trying to not get too bogged down by other people’s expectations of the show. I know it’s beloved, but that doesn’t scare me — that excites me.” Adds Gruska: “Making sure we are telling that story, honoring the tone of the movie, and being free to push it forward and be ourselves has been a wonderful and rewarding challenge.” Most listened to cast album “Jesus Christ Superstar” (Jepsen) Go-to Broadway karaoke song “Maria” from “West Side Story” (Gruska); “On the Street Where You Live” from “My Fair Lady” (Jepsen) First Broadway show “Spamalot” (Gruska) Ryo Kamibayashi, Ashlyn Maddox, Tyler Jordan Wesley, Amalia Yoo, ‘Spring Awakening’ Twenty years after “Spring Awakening” launched the careers of Lea Michele and Jonathan Groff, a new generation is getting its turn. Thousands of performers responded to an open casting call before Kamibayashi, Maddox, Jordan Wesley and Yoo emerged as the leads of the Off Broadway revival. “It was like the Hunger Games of New York,” jokes Kamibayashi, who plays Moritz, the troubled schoolboy. “I skipped Jury Duty to go to my first appointment!” says Maddox, who plays the leading naïve Wendela. The foursome came to auditions with varying familiarity with the show and were encouraged to “approach it like it’s a new work,” says Yoo, who plays the free-spirited Ilse. “It hasn’t been done with people who look like us, people with our lived experiences.” For Wesley, who plays the rebellious lead Melchior, that opportunity is personal: “Having been a little Black boy from South Carolina seeing this industry and being like, ‘I want to carve out a piece of this for me’ … to be realizing that with this show is very cool.” None of the four has connected with their predecessors yet, though Wesley is looking forward to meeting Groff. “I know that he’s a Beyoncé lover. I also love Beyoncé, so I think we’ll hit it off there,” he says. And if history repeats itself? Kamibayashi jokes, “Hopefully we all get to book our version of ‘Glee’ after this.” Dream shows or roles on Broadway Bobby in “Company” or George in “Sunday in the Park With George” (Kamibayashi); “Carnival” (Maddox); Judas in “Jesus Christ Superstar” (Jordan Wesley); the Witch in “Into the Woods” or Mary Todd Lincoln in “Oh, Mary!” (Yoo) Liisi LaFontaine, ‘Wanted’ LaFontaine is one-half of the duo at the center of the new musical “Wanted” — a Western about biracial sisters who pass for white and rob their way through 1893 Texas. “Hot — sign me up!” LaFontaine jokes. But it was the “depth and truth” of the story that captivated her. After leading West End productions of “Dreamgirls” and “Moulin Rouge!,” LaFontaine is making her Broadway debut this season at the James Earl Jones Theatre. “I’ve been working towards this moment for the last decade,” she says. “I’m just kicking my feet.” LaFontaine has been developing the role of Martha since the show’s earliest iterations, alongside now co-star and “twin flame” Solea Pfeiffer. Playing the biracial sisters has allowed the pair to unpack questions about their own identities. “It feels like we get to represent ancestors we didn’t know we had,” LaFontaine says. Martha and her sister, Mary, are based on the real-life great-great-aunts of book writer and lyricist Angelica Chéri, giving LaFontaine a “direct line” to their history — and a particular responsibility in bringing Martha to the stage. “I feel an immense pressure to get it right, but I also feel so much freedom knowing people don’t know her yet and I’m the one chosen to introduce her to the world,” she says. “Creating a character is such a gift, but also a very different kind of responsibility.” First Broadway show “I saw my mom play Sarah in ‘Ragtime’ when I was 3 and scream-cried because I thought she got killed onstage.” Show that needs a revival “Aida” Whitney Leavitt, ‘Just in Time’ Leavitt became famous on reality television as the breakout star of “The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives” and later on “Dancing With the Stars,” but she secretly dreamed of performing on Broadway. Though she grew up as a competitive dancer, she abandoned her acting ambitions to become a stay-at-home mom. Still, she made her Broadway debut last year in “Chicago” as Roxie Hart, and her run broke the box office record for highest weekly sales in the show’s nearly 30-year history. “I walked into the Ambassador Theatre hoping I could do the role, and I left that experience wanting even more,” Leavitt says. She didn’t have to wait long for her next gig. In December, Leavitt is returning to the stage in the Bobby Darin musical “Just in Time” as singer Sandra Dee. “I wanted my next role to challenge me and feel completely different from ‘Chicago,’” says Leavitt. “I’ve experienced people forming opinions about me based on pieces of my life, and Sandra’s story made me think about how important it is to protect the parts of yourself that are yours.” Leavitt’s pivot from reality TV to theater is notable because she’s bringing new audiences to Broadway. “That’s one of my favorite parts of this experience,” she says. “If someone came because they knew me from TikTok, ‘Secret Lives’ or ‘Dancing With the Stars’ and left loving Broadway, that’s a win. Because once you see one, you’re going to want to see them all!” First Broadway show “Hairspray” Go-to Broadway karaoke song “If They Could See Me Now” from “Sweet Charity” Theater superstition you believe “Not wishing someone good luck before they go to stage; I don’t want to hear that!” Show that needs a revival “Guys and Dolls” Nathan Levy, ‘The Fantasticks’ Levy isn’t new to Broadway — he has four shows under his belt — but his fifth feels different. “Just now, with this show and with this role, I’m finally arriving,” he says. “It’s all starting to make sense.” This fall, Levy will originate Lewis in the Broadway debut of “The Fantasticks,” more than 65 years after the musical premiered Off Broadway. The new production reimagines the central romance as a queer love story, turning Luisa — a role traditionally played by a soprano — into Lewis. For Levy, that gender-bend allows him the freedom to explore the character separately from those who’ve come before him. “It’s essentially a new role, so I can just sort of approach it as that,” he says. “It could be super intimidating to go down the rabbit hole and see all the great women, all the great sopranos, that have come before me. But it’s nice and refreshing to know that we’re switching it up.” The change also gives the decades-old love story a new perspective. “It’s really refreshing to see a queer love story these days where the sexuality is not necessarily the struggle or the main conflict,” Levy says. “It just is.” First Broadway show “Newsies,” with “The Fantasticks” choreographer Christopher Gattelli Go-to karaoke song “Bohemian Rhapsody” or something from “Legally Blonde” Show that needs a revival “Bye Bye Birdie” Mason Alexander Park, ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ After lighting up the West End in productions of “Cabaret,” “Oh, Mary!” and “The Tempest,” Park, who’s nonbinary, is making their Broadway debut as Margaret in “Much Ado About Nothing.” “I think London has finally had enough of me,” Park cracks. Director Jamie Lloyd’s revival of Shakespeare’s comedy, starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell, drew raves on the West End. During that production, Park learned the importance of taking the work, but not themself, seriously. “We are so fortunate to get to make fools of ourselves amongst talented friends for a living, so might as well enjoy as much of it as possible,” they say. Having acted in two Shakespeare plays, Park is no longer intimidated by the material: “There’s so much room for interpretation and play, might as well take a big swing. The legacy of his work should liberate you rather than scare you.” If Park does get nervous about a project, they remember their favorite piece of advice: “Embrace your singularity. If they wanted someone else, they’d just call them to do it instead.” Most listened to cast album “Hedwig and the Angry Inch” Show they’re most excited to see this season “Evita” Dream show “Kiss of the Spider Woman” Zoe Sarnak and Michael Weiner, ‘Galileo’ Image Credit: Courtesy Image Sarnak and Weiner’s first writing session started like a jam. “She picked up her guitar. I go to the piano. We talk; we sing together, band style,” Weiner says. “It kind of evolves really organically from there, just going back and forth.” The first-time collaborators wrote the music and lyrics for “Galileo,” a musical about the father of modern science. The show marks Sarnak’s Broadway debut and Weiner’s first Broadway musical since 2013’s “First Date.” Their style of collaboration — a “yes, and” approach, as Sarnak describes it — has helped them create a score that gives each character a distinct musical identity. For Galileo, the answer was rock. “He felt like a rock star in his generation — one of those rebellious people who would challenge authority — which is what rock music is all about,” Weiner says. Sarnak has her own connection to the material. The daughter of a scientist, she double majored in molecular biology and music before pursuing songwriting. “I have always felt that math and science minds, they’re artists, they’re dreamers,” she says. “They see the world in this unexpected, outside-of-the-box, expansive way.” First Broadway show “A Chorus Line” at the Shubert Theatre (Weiner); “Guys and Dolls” or “Chicago” (Sarnak) Taylor Swift Announces New Single, ‘Patient Zero,’ Coming This Week There Is Precedent for Taylor Swift’s ‘Cleveland!’ Making the World Go Crazy: Paul McCartney’s ‘Silly Love Songs’ Era Emmys: A Breakdown of the Music Nominees From Lady Gaga’s ‘Dead Dance’ to Hans Zimmer’s Race for His First Win Travis Kelce Breaks Down Wedding to Taylor Swift and Says Adam Sandler Officiating Was ‘Absolutely Insane’: ‘He’s the F—ing Best Person on This Planet’ Country Songs Take All Five Slots in the Billboard Hot 100’s Top 5 for the First Time in Chart History Tom Cruise Says Taylor Swift Was ‘Schooling Me on Football’ at Chiefs Game, Calls Her a ‘Brilliant Musician and Director’ Loading comments...

title: Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere
full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere Oscars: Pakistan Picks Mo Naqvi’s Doc Thriller ‘Hanging By A Wire’ As Best International Feature Entry ‘Musk’ Director Alex Gibney On World’s Richest Man: “He’s A Bullsh*tter” View All October 2, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Drug in Our Pocket' Obscured Releasing EXCLUSIVE: Obscured Releasing has acquired North American distribution rights to The Drug in Our Pocket , a documentary by Anne Sundberg about the pernicious effects on young people of constant smartphone use. The feature produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg holds its world premiere Saturday at the Hamptons International Film Festival in New York, and heads from there to the Heartland International Film Festival in Indianapolis and the Newport Beach Film Festival in Southern California. The Drug in Our Pocket is expected to get an Oscar-qualifying run this fall, followed by a limited theatrical release in early 2027. Related Stories Acquisitions Obscured Releasing Takes North America To Emily Robinson's SXSW Horror Pic 'Ugly Cry' News Sian Clifford Satirical Comedy 'Lady' Scores U.S. Deal “ The Drug in Our Pocket examines how smartphones, designed to connect us, have radically reshaped childhood, adolescence, and mental health,” notes a release. “Through intimate conversations with young people, parents, and leading experts, the film reveals a generation that is thoughtful, articulate, and increasingly aware of how digital environments shape their attention, emotions, and sense of self.” Watch on Deadline The documentary premieres as dozens of states have banned or restricted the use of cell phones in schools, recognizing the impact of the devices on student mental health. Similarly, several countries including Australia, France, Greece, Malaysia, and Brazil have moved to ban or restrict teen access to social media. From Instagram “With The Drug in Our Pocket , director Anne Sundberg brilliantly weaves psychological expert interviews, behind-the-scenes stories from tech whistleblowers, and deeply personal accounts of teenagers and parents exposing how big tech and our government have failed us,” said RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler of Obscured Releasing. “This is a necessary call to action highlighting the impact of social media and technology which offers us the steps we can take to reclaim our power, and attention.” Sundberg’s credits includes four films co-directed with Ricki Stern: The Trials of Darryl Hunt , Joan Rivers: A Piece of Work , The Devil Came on Horseback , and Reversing Roe . Director Anne Sundberg Courtesy of HamptonsFilm In a statement, Sundberg said, “RJ and Bill are brilliant at connecting films to audiences. They understood that for us, The Drug in Our Pocket isn’t just about documenting young people’s experiences growing up online. They share our vision that this film can start a larger movement asking us all to pay attention to our attention. We are thrilled to be working with them on this release.” The acquisition deal was negotiated by Anne Sundberg and Beth Kojima on behalf of the production and Bill Guentzler and RJ Millard on behalf of Obscured Releasing. The Drug in Our Pocket is directed by Anne Sundberg and produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg. Kojima, Sundberg, and John Wayland wrote the film. Wayland edited the documentary. Timo Elliston and Brian Jones composed the score. Executive producers include Regina K. Scully, Jenna Bush Hager, Crystal McCrary McGuire, Ashley Graham, Lizzie Tisch, and Jonathan Tisch. Obscured Releasing Obscured Releasing was launched by RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler in 2025 “to build film-first distribution strategies that prioritize collaboration in order to engage audiences through festival play, publicity and promotional campaigns, theatrical runs, and thoughtful VOD release windows.” Among its titles are Blue Film , starring Reed Birney and Kieron Moore; Siobhan McCarthy’s trans high school comedy She’s the He ; Christian Nilsson’s Westhampton , starring Finn Wittrock, RJ Mitte, Jake Weary, Amy Forsyth, and Tovah Feldshuh. Documentary releases include Stop The Insanity: Finding Susan Powter , and Endless Cookie . title: How ‘DWTS’ Pro Hailey Bills Is Using Her Nepo Baby Status to Dance Her Way to the Top
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close Hailey Bills Photograph by Aria Askari As one of only five dancers throughout Dancing With the Stars ‘ history to be promoted from troupe to pro after just one season, Hailey Bills has every right to brag. But that’s not Bills’ style, as she’s just grateful to have made the little dancer growing up in Utah who had big dreams proud. “I haven’t really come to terms with where [and] what my life is,” Bills tells The Hollywood Reporter over a recent Zoom from her trailer outside Los Angeles’ Television City, where the show tapes. “When I see people on the streets and they’re saying, ‘Oh my gosh, are you Hailey Bills?’ I’m like, how on earth do you know who I am? It’s so weird.” Related Stories TV 'Big Brother' Reveals Season 28 Winner: See Who Won the Game (and America's Favorite Houseguest) TV The Record-Breaking 'Celebrity Traitors' U.K. Is Back for Season 2: Where to Watch Online From the States Last year, Bills joined the DWTS dance troupe, a group of dancers who perform supplemental, non-competitive numbers and are not paired with celebrities. After season 34 wrapped in November 2025, she headed out on tour in January for five months, performing alongside the pros as if she was one of them. While she didn’t have pro status just yet, there’s no denying she was already catching people’s attention through the screen and on the road. Bills has since amassed a combined million followers across social platforms, proving to be a bona fide reality and social media star. The DWTS producers clearly noticed. Just as Bills was jumping back into the swing of things on tour, she was told “literally minutes before” one of their performances this past spring that she’d be a pro on season 35. That meant after just one season in the troupe, whereas other pros have spent five seasons before being upped, she would take on her first year competing and teaching a star how to perform ballroom dance. Bills was caught by surprise. “People think I’m lying when I say this; I was not expecting it at all. Like, truly, I was not,” she admits. It’s not shocking that some are skeptical of Bills’ honesty — she skyrocketed as a beloved figure in the DWTS community after her troupe tenure, boosted by her presence in the franchise after appearing on the Juniors spinoff in 2018 alongside her aunt, mirrorball champion Jenna Johnson . However, she also questioned her chances at a promotion due to the new franchise entry DWTS: The Next Pro , which confirmed another new dancer would be added for season 35 onto the already long recurring cast list (and Bills wasn’t competing for that spot). “I was on tour this past year with DWTS , and that’s when they were filming The Next Pro . I thought there was just no way [I’d become a pro] with this Next Pro show happening,” she says. “And I was totally fine with that. I was just praying that I would be asked back on troupe.” Once Bills’ pro casting was confirmed by ABC , it was monumental in itself, as she became part of DWTS ‘ second-ever all-female partnership, being coupled with Sarah Jane Nader, the third-ever same-sex pairing. Bills and Nader’s partnership is also a casting wink; Johnson became the first female pro to be partnered with a woman back in 2021 when she danced with Jojo Siwa. There was pressure on Bills’ shoulders heading into the season 35 premiere; it was her pro debut, and the second time two women would perform as a pair on the ABC program. Her season was unfortunately short-lived, as Bills and Nader were eliminated during the second premiere episode, where only the female celebrities performed. She has no hard feelings about her elimination, but wishes she had more time to showcase what she’s really like as a pro. “I think I speak for me and Adele [Zaikman, the Next Pro winner who was also booted during the first premiere night] when I say we wish we would have had more time to showcase [our talents]. But we also understand that there has to be someone to go, and that’s just how it was this season,” she says while chatting with THR nearly two weeks after being eliminated. It was important for Bills to shift her mindset from the disappointment that came with her elimination into gratitude. She admits “it is a hard balance,” juggling wanting to take the competition seriously while also keeping things light. Adele Zaikman and Hailey Bills perform on Dancing With the Stars . Disney/Christopher Willard “It’s so hard, because this is such a life-consuming thing, to do this show. When I got cut, of course that’s a sad thing, and it was a hard night,” Bills says. “We were sad, disappointed, and all the things. But at the end of the day, I am choosing not to let it beat me up, because I still have 10 weeks on the show, and I could choose to be sad about it, or I can choose to just move on, because there truly isn’t anything I can do about it.” Bills has been dancing since her childhood; her parents initially “made sure to put me in all the sports.” Between soccer, flag football, gymnastics and dance, she had her heart set on pursuing either soccer and dance at seven years old. She chose the latter, partly due to her familiar ties to the craft. “A factor that went into that [choice] is my family,” she says. “A lot of my family members are dancers. My aunt [Jenna], my mom, my other aunt.” Bills hails from Utah’s Center Stage Performing Arts Studio, which she jokes is “a big breeder of all these DWTS pros.” She’s not wrong, as a whopping nine former and current Dancing pros trained at the studio (including host Julianne Hough and her brother, judge Derek Hough). Bills was dancing at Center Stage when ABC began casting for Juniors ; she also doesn’t shy away from her aunt playing a part in her being cast. “Of course, I work so hard in dance, but I think a huge factor into me being on the show is my aunt being Jenna Johnson ,” she says. “I have to give her the credit for that.” She’s not the only DWTS pro to reap the benefits of her family tree; fellow pro Rylee Arnold is the younger sister to season 25 winner Lindsay Arnold; Bills’ uncle, Val Chmerkovskiy, was brought in as a pro after his brother Maks joined in season two; and Derek was cast after Julianne won her first year as a pro in season four. “This is a cast of nepo babies,” she says when asked if the interconnectivity of the DWTS pros makes the cast one of nepotism. “I’m proud to say I’m a nepo baby… I think a lot of us are.” Below, Bills opens up about what she learned from her fast first season as a DWTS pro, the advice Mark Ballas gave her that she holds close, her quick rise to acclaim as a dancer and more. You are one of many pros who have connections to other pros from the show. Do you think that makes the cast of Dancing With the Stars a cast of nepotism? Oh my gosh, 1,000 percent. Like, I won’t even try to deny it. No, I’m proud to say I’m a nepo baby. Like, it’s just how it works, and I think a lot of us are, and that’s so lucky for us. I think I’m lucky to be a nepo baby. I’m lucky to have connections, but I don’t want that to downplay the fact that I and other people have worked really, really, really hard to get into this position. 1,000 percent; this is a cast of nepo babies, but I will say we’ve all worked extremely hard. I love that you carry such a good attitude about that. Why is it important for you to embrace it? I think it’s coming to terms with the fact that it’s just true. I don’t know how I would have gotten on the show if my aunt weren’t Jenna. Who knows if I would have? Truly, I don’t know. But I know that that came into place, and I know that because I had a connection with her, I was presented this role a little bit easier than others would. So I’m just gonna accept that. I’m really grateful for that, and I’m lucky. Hailey Bills and Sarah Jane Nader perform on the Dancing With the Stars season 35 premiere. Disney/Eric McCandless Is there anything you’ve learned as your first year as a pro that you want to take into your next season? I genuinely feel like a changed person after this experience. But I think walking in, if I am lucky enough to be a pro next season, I’ll know a lot more. Just starting from the ground up: how that works, patience levels and adapting to your partner’s learning style. Do you have any unique or special hobbies or talents? I wouldn’t even say this is a talent; this is a hobby that I’m trying to be good at. I’ve been trying to get into piano. I’m, like, obsessed with it. I really want to be good at it. So, with all this free time that I’m having [after being eliminated], I might start doing lessons. I also love reading. I am obsessed with reading right now. I love hiking, being outdoors. Sometimes I’ll go rent a bike or a scooter, and just go be free. What does your perfect day off look like? I wake up, sleep in a little bit, of course, and then go get breakfast. Maybe get a croissant or some sort of pastry. Go work out, because I love working out, and then I would dance for a little bit; I would just go sesh it out. Maybe bring someone with me to do that, and then I would go to the pool, be outdoors. Go to dinner with my friends, watch a movie, have a game night, go to bed. What is something you can absolutely not live without? An unserious thing is Diet Coke. I actually can’t function without Diet Coke, so that’s not healthy and not good. Do you have a favorite thing that you have ever stolen from the Dancing With the Stars set? I am obsessed with hoop earrings. I will always have a hoop earring in, and one time when I was on troupe, I had the cutest silver rhinestone earrings, and I decided to keep them on when I went home. Hailey Bills for Dancing With the Stars season 35. Disney/Andrew Eccles What is the best piece of advice you have received that you’ve actually used? It was from Mark Ballas, actually a couple months ago. It’s just really stuck with me, and he said to me, “I want you to remember, it’s not that serious, but it is, also.” It’s a good message to me that when you need to be in it and lock in, absolutely do that and be 100 percent in. But also, if it doesn’t go your way, it’s not the end of the world. It’s just not that serious, and you shouldn’t let that kill you, and you just need to move on. Having found success and fame now after two years on Dancing With the Stars , is it what you expected to be? Have you been able to process it yet? Honestly, I don’t think so. I haven’t really come to terms with where [and] what my life is. It’s been such a switch. I feel like now that I was announced being a pro, and when I see people on the streets and they’re saying, “Oh my gosh, are you Hailey Bills?” I’m like, how on earth do you know who I am? It’s so weird, but it’s been a big switch-up. I think now, finally, I’m like, OK, this is what life is, and this is how we just need to live. I think I’m processing it a little bit, but I’m still in denial in a good way. THR

title: ‘A Different World’ Earns Fast Season 2 Renewal at Netflix
full_text: Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 7:30am From left: Alijah Kai, Maleah Joi Moon and Kennedi Reece in 'A Different World.' Daniel Delgado Jr/Netflix Logo text Netflix ‘s report card on A Different World is a good one: The streamer has renewed the show for a second season. The renewal for the show, a sequel to the 1980s-90s NBC sitcom, was a quick one. Netflix announced the season two order just eight days after A Different World’ s Sept. 24 debut. The second season will follow Deborah (Maleah Joi Moon) and her Hillman College classmates into their sophomore years. “It’s so validating to be bolstered by our amazing audience. We are beyond excited to return to Hillman and continue to tell meaningful and heartfelt stories that resonate across generations,” creator and showrunner Felicia Pride said in a statement. “I am thrilled for our brilliant cast and our hard-working crew.” Related Stories TV Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul to Lead Series Comms at Netflix TV Ted Sarandos Explains Why the 'Stranger Things' Team Left Netflix A Different World collected 4.2 million views and 23 million hours of watch time worldwide in its first four days of release, according to Netflix’s internal data. The series centers on Moon’s Deborah, the youngest child of Whitley Gilbert and Dwayne Wayne (original series stars Jasmine Guy and Kadeem Hardison), as she follows in her parents’ footsteps at Hillman, a historically Black college. “Halleluja! The people and Netflix have spoken,” said director and executive producer Debbie Allen. “ A Different World brought something everybody needed: joy, romance, relevance, authenticity, and heart.” Added Tracey Pakosta, vp comedy series at Netflix, “We are so excited to see how audiences around the world have embraced the next chapter of this beloved series. We believed in this incredible team from day one, and can’t wait to see what unfolds next year at Hillman College.” Pride told The Hollywood Reporter that she grew up with the original series and wanted to “capture and imbue the spirit” of it in the Netflix show. “The feeling that it gave you, which for me, was warmth,” she said. “The feeling of having this community of students and friends and mentors and elders, also the texture and the culture of HBCUs, and then the political consciousness of the show. Those were the sides of the square.” Along with Moon, Guy and Hardison, the show’s cast includes Alijah Kai, Cornell Young IV, Jordan Aaron Hall, Kennedi Reece, Chibuikem Uche and original series actors Cree Summer and Darryl M. Bell. Jada Pinkett Smith, Glynn Turman, Joe Morton, Jenifer Lewis, Karen Malina White, Ajai Sanders and Charnele Brown had guest appearances in season one, reprising their roles from the NBC show. Pride executive produces A Different World with Allen, Tom Werner , Reggie Rock Bythewood , Gina Prince-Bythewood and Mandy Summers. THR
