title: IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’
full_text: Oct 2, 2026 7:24am PT IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’ By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest IDF Slams ‘NAZA,’ Saying It Presents a ‘Distorted, Misleading and Disingenuous Picture’ 1 hour ago ITV Boss, Sky’s Content Chief Set Out Vision for Acquisition, Try to Calm Nerves: ‘The Competition is Ferocious’ 3 days ago Graham Norton Shoots Down ‘Conspiracy Theory’ That Taylor Swift’s ‘Opalite’ Video Was Shot Before She Came on His Show 3 days ago See All Courtesy MK2 The Israeli Defense Forces has slammed the documentary “ NAZA ,” calling it “manipulative,” “misleading” and “based on substantial factual errors.” The film premiered at Venice Film Festival last month, where it received a 24.5-minute standing ovation. It has since screened at the San Sebastián and New York film festivals, and will open in U.S. theaters next week before streaming for free on The Guardian website in late November. The British newspaper are co-producers of the movie, which is directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor. Related Stories Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Lobbying Group Amid Backlash Over Cost of Sports on Streaming Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale In its statement, the IDF said that it did not have a chance to view the documentary prior to its premiere and claimed the directors did not put forward the allegations in the film to the IDF before publishing. The IDF has now responded to the numerous claims in the film, which takes its title from the phrase “collateral damage” in Hebrew (“Nezek Agavi”). Popular on Variety Among other points, the IDF said that it operates under binding directives that “explicitly” distinguish between military operatives and uninvolved citizens; it has never planned or carried out a strike in Gaza in which 500 civilians were killed, as one anonymous contributor claims in the film; and it has never used AI to select targets to strike, saying these are only ever planned by “relevant professionals.” All 24 contributors in “NAZA” are anonymous, filmed against a nighttime skyline in Tel Aviv. In its statement, the IDF said “it is apparent that in various cases interviewees raise speculation and assumptions without a factual basis.” They added that the filmmakers also left out crucial context such as showing the full chain of command, which they said includes roles dedicated to “mitigating civilian harm,” and played down the Oct. 7 attacks on Israel, in which over 1,000 people were killed and over 250 hostages were taken. “The film ‘NAZA’ presents a distorted, misleading and disingenuous picture of the IDF’s target planning and striking process,” the statement reads. “The film’s narrative is based on substantial factual errors stemming from manipulative misrepresentations of reality.” Contacted by Variety for comment, a spokesperson for Guardian News & Media said on behalf of the filmmakers: “The IDF’s attempt to portray the 24 participants in ‘NAZA’ as junior-ranking officers involved only in the early stages of the targeting process is false. They include officers and soldiers who were involved in multiple stages of the targeting process in Gaza, including intelligence, operations and the final authorization process.” The Guardian added that “the process of assessing the credibility of the testimonies was rigorous. It included leaked classified documents, detailed verification of specific strikes and corroboration via a wider pool of confidential journalistic sources who did not appear on camera in the film. Over the past three years we have together interviewed more than 100 sources familiar with IDF systems used in the war in Gaza, including senior-ranking commanders directly involved in the authorization of strikes.” The statement concluded: “The Guardian stands fully behind the film, which builds on three years of detailed reporting by the Guardian and our partners. title: Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit,  Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit
full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony TIFF Midnight Madness Hit ‘River’ Gets Winter 2027 Date From Blumhouse Atomic Monster ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Worldwide Opening As Box Office Braces For ‘Digger’ Impact – Global Preview ‘Ebenezer’ Trailer: Johnny Depp Leads Ti West’s Dickens Remake View All October 2, 2026 7:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc L-R: Josh Greenstein, Dana Goldberg, Michael De Luca, and Pam Abdy Skydance/Courtesy The soon to be merged Paramount Warner Bros Motion Picture unit under the freshly labeled Skydance is bound to be run by current Paramount Motion Picture co-chairs, Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg , multiple sources say. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs This comes after a sleepless night for Warner Bros’ Motion Picture Chairs Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy , who we hear, first learned that they weren’t making the jump to the new company from reports last night. It’s our understanding that Paramount co-CEO David Ellison never made a phone call to them about their future and whether or not there’s a job offer in hand. The news comes at a stinging time, as Warner Bros’ faces an epic flop in the $125M-$160M+ priced Tom Cruise starring, Alejandro Iñárritu social satire, Digger, which is poised to open to around $30M WW or less this weekend. De Luca and Abdy have been at Warner Bros since June 2022, when they jumped over from MGM following Amazon’s acquisition of that storied studio. The duo recently re-upped their contracts under WBD CEO David Zaslav through 2030. Key to their future at the new Paramount Warner Bros is whether or not Ellison continued to honor their current terms, which would have Warner Bros marketing and distribution departments report into them. From the sounds of it, those are tough terms for the numbers-crunching Ellison to honor. He’s a loyalist to his 16-year production colleague Goldberg, and longtime amigo Greenstein who have been steering the motion picture unit into financially reasonable shape following the old Paramount. Watch on Deadline Paramount will inherit a combined slate around 71 dated features through 2028, 56% of that generated by De Luca and Abdy’s Warner Bros. There’s still more to be dated by both studios in 2028. Paramount will also gain a film library that includes the $4.37 billion global grossing 2025 slate that De Luca and Abdy built as well as Oscar winners One Battle After Another, Sinners (until the rights of that film revert to its director Ryan Coogler) and Weapons. In addition, the new Paramount is looking at a potential $1 billion-grossing year-end holiday tentpole in Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune: Part Three. There appears to be some talks as to exactly what De Luca and Abdy’s role will be in the new entity, however, the duo weren’t contracted to report into other motion picture chairs, rather the CEO. Reporting into Greenstein and Goldberg doesn’t sound like a likely scenario for the duo per sources. De Luca and Abdy could be offered a producing contract in the new Skydance. The executive chart for the new Paramount Warner Bros is expected to be announced in a matter of days. Ellison brought in former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. “Ellison will focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including its talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation,” Paramount said. “Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day management and integration of the combined businesses.” There was an optimistic buzz on Thursday that De Luca and Abdy would also have gate rights on the Melrose lot, and potentially report into Kreiz, but that’s not the likely scenario. Additionally in the new Paramount Warner Bros as of late, Casey Bloys was tapped as streaming head of the combined Paramount-WBD with Paramount’s current Chair of Direct-to-Consumer, Cindy Holland departing. Mark Thompson was told he’d stay on to oversee CNN going forward. While De Luca and Abdy had a great run at the box office last year, this year has been littered with myriad misfires including The Bride, Supergirl with no movie earning more than $100M stateside. The total domestic box office for Jan. 1-Oct. 1 is $448.4M. However, Paramount, too, hasn’t had a great box office year, their current domestic box office YTD right behind Warners with $429.8M, however, they had two $100M+ domestic titles in Scream 7 and Miramax’s Scary Movie. At the year-to-date North American box office, the newly combined Paramount Warner Bros would count $878.2M ranking behind Universal ($1.8B), Disney ($1.55B) and Sony ($1.28B). Under De Luca and Abdy, Warner Bros tallied 30 noms earlier this year, which tied the studio’s record from 2005. Warners took home 11 of those Oscars (six including Best Picture for One Battle After Another , four for Sinners, and supporting actress Amy Madigan’s win for Weapons ). The two had a reputation for protecting filmmakers’ vision, and were audacious in bankrolling auteur projects like Paul Thomas Anderson’s most expensive movie ever, the $140M One Battle After Another and Coogler’s $90M period vampire musical Sinners. One Battle After Another wound up being Anderson’s highest grossing movie ever at $213M+ at the global box office, though film finance sources questioned its profitability. Sinners was a great success with close to $372M WW. De Luca and Abdy presided over MGM starting in January 2020 until April 2022. There they built a slate which assisted in fueling the studio’s sale to Amazon for $8.45 billion for the 4,000 title library. During their run there, theatrical releases included No Time to Die, House of Gucci, Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza, not to mention they teed up Creed III, which became the highest-grossing in that franchise and the second-highest-grossing in the Rocky franchise. Paramount could not be reached for comment. title: SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Keanu Reeves, Seth Rogen, Gemma Chan and Jordan Firstman Among Big Names Set for Honors (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 7:11am Gemma Chan, John Cho, Carrie Coon, Rosalind Eleazar, Jordan Firstman, James Gray, Anthony Ippolito, Billie Piper, Keanu Reeves and Seth Rogen Courtesy of Subject (4); Benjo Arwas; Heather Hazzan; Will Aldersley; Macrae Marran; Simon Emmett; Brian Bowen Smith Later this month, a veritable parade of A-list movie stars and filmmakers — many of whom are in serious contention for Oscars — will head south to attend screenings of their work and collect special honors at the 29th edition of the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , the nation’s largest university-run film festival. The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report that they will include Josephine supporting actress/producer Gemma Chan (Lumiere Award); Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother supporting actor John Cho (Luminary Award); The Liberation lead actress Carrie Coon (Luminary Award); Misty Green lead actress Rosalind Eleazar (Breakthrough Award); Club Kid writer/director/lead actor Jordan Firstman (Rising Star Director Award); Paper Tiger writer/director/producer James Gray (Auteur Award); I Play Rocky lead actor Anthony Ippolito (Breakthrough Award); Backrooms director Kane Parsons (Next Gen Award); Elsinore supporting actress Billie Piper (Marquee Award); and The Invite supporting actor Seth Rogen (Spotlight Award). Related Stories Movies SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Directors of 10 of 2026's Top Documentaries Set for 'Docs to Watch' Panel (Exclusive) Movies Mariska Hargitay Is Still Processing Her Devastating Doc About Her Mother: "It's Like a Psychic Surgery" Additionally, the four principal stars of Peter Berg’s WWII drama The Mosquito Bowl — Tom Francis, Nicholas Galitzine, Ray Nicholson and Bill Skarsgärd — will be presented with the fest’s Ensemble Award. And beloved screen veteran Keanu Reeves will be presented with the Legend of Cinema Award at a screening of The Matrix , and will separately participate in a panel about BRZRKR , a comic book series that he co-wrote, alongside co-writer Matt Kindt and illustrator Ron Garney. title: Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros.
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:57am Pamela Abdy and Michael De Luca attend the 'Digger' London premiere. Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy are out at Warner Bros, an insider tells The Hollywood Reporter . The news of film chiefs’ imminent exit comes as Paramount Skydance prepares for its landmark $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. The combined David Ellison-owned super studio is now called, simply, Skydance, with the merger expected to be finalized on Oct. 6. Paramount film heads Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein are expected to oversee both movie studios. Abdy and De Luca are said to have told associates they have been in talks for a possible next act at Netflix. De Luca and Abdy‘s tenure heading up Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group began in 2022 and has been marked by highs and lows. The highs have included box office successes like the Minecraft Movie ($960 million, globally) and Ryan Coogler’s Sinners ($370 million, globally), along with critical achievements like last year’s Oscars best picture win for Paul Thomas Anderson‘s One Battle After Another and other wins for Sinners . The misfires have included expensive swings like Maggie Gyllenhaal‘s The Bride! and Tom Cruise starrer Digger , which is tracking to open this weekend to a dismal $8 million to $15 million on a $125 million-plus budget. De Luca and Abdy joined Warner Bros. from MGM, where they oversaw that storied studio’s film slate for two years until its 2022 $8.5 billion acquisition by Amazon Prime Video. At Warners, they inherited a slate from the previous regime, headed by Toby Emmerich, that included Legendary’s Dune franchise and the box office hit Barbie , along with Bong Joon Ho‘s Mickey 17 and Robert De Niro starrer The Alto Knights , the latter of which was personally greenlit by Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav. As for their own auspices, the duo is known for being director-friendly, offering a big studio home (and big studio budgets) to filmmakers like Anderson, Coogler, Alejandro Iñárritu and Emerald Fennell. The auteur-driven titles were buffeted by a series of IP plays and franchise offerings, predominantly hailing from the studio’s New Line division, De Luca’s longtime stomping grounds, like the well-received Final Destination reboot and a Conjuring installment. De Luca and Abdy’s exit comes amid a flurry of other executive announcements at the soon-to-be-combined studio. Earlier this week, Cindy Holland exited her post as Paramount Skydance’s streaming chief, with HBO boss Casey Bloys expected to lead all streaming efforts at the combined studios. Also this week, it was announced that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz would come on as co-CEO with Ellison. Puck first reported the news of De Luca and Abdy‘s exit. THR

title: Canal+ Calls VAT Hike “A Direct Attack” On Its Operations In France As Guilds Protest Move
full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie CANEX Creations CEO Osahon Akpata Talks Mission To Shake Up Film Finance in Africa: “There Is A Huge Opportunity To Create IP That’s An Investable Class” Kelli Garner & Michael Stahl-David To Co-Star In Romantic Road Movie ‘You Always’ Dark Sky Films Takes U.S. Rights To Prize-Winning Emirati Horror ‘The Vile’ View All October 2, 2026 6:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Canal+ HQ in Boulogne Billancourt Getty Images Paris-based pay-TV giant Canal+ has hit back at the French government’s plan to double the VAT rate on TV subscriptions from 10% to 20% saying it could leave a potential €200M ($225M) hole in its finances. The planned hike was confirmed in a draft budget plan for 2027 presented by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Thursday. The controversial package aimed at reining in France ’s public debt, with the government says is poised to hit a record 121.7% of domestic product (GDP) in 2027, proposes some €43B ($48B) worth of “recovery measures” which include increasing revenue from VAT. Related Stories News David Michel Buys Cottonwood Media Out Of Federation Studios News YouTube Says 'Obsession' & 'Backrooms' Point To Awards Future For Films Born On The Platform In a separate development, the budget plan also includes a proposal to cut to a tax deduction for YouTube , YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and Instagram linked to payments they make to France’s National Cinema Centre (CNC). Watch on Deadline These platforms were integrated in 2016 into France’s virtuous system of obligations, under which all entities distributing content in the territory are required to pay a percentage of their local revenue to the CNC, which is then put back into the local film and TV industry. Up until now, the obligation was based on around 35% of their advertising revenues thanks to 66% “abatement” but this has been halved. The measure is expected to raise around €60M ($60M) Canal+ reaction Canal+ called the decision to double the VAT rate for TV subscriptions “inconsistent” and “ill-advised”, noting that the government had only just last year confirmed that the 10% rate would stay in place. “If adopted, this measure would have a massive negative impact on the Group’s revenue and operating margin, potentially reaching €200 million annually, while the revenue gain for the State would amount to less than a quarter of that figure,” read a statement from the pay-TV giant. “Canal+ would be unable to absorb such a loss in France and would consequently be forced to adjust its operations in mainland France and the Overseas Territories. This would inevitably impact subscription prices, workforce levels, and financial contributions to the film and sports ecosystems—and the creative sector more broadly. The film and rugby communities have already rightly raised alarms regarding the risks this measure poses to the future of their respective industries.” Canal+, which floated on the London Stock Exchange in 2024 as part of a restructuring by Vivendi and has also expanded its footprint in Africa with the acquisition of the MultiChoice Group last year, said the VAT hike in France would lead it to double down on its international activities. “With operations now spanning nearly 70 countries, Canal+ regrets this direct attack on its business in its home market of France; it will draw the necessary conclusions and accelerate its international expansion strategy,” said the pay-TV. Industry reaction Rumors of the proposed VAT regime change for Canal+ had already sparked alarm bells with the French film and TV sectors earlier this week. Canal+ is one of the France’s major backers of local and European films and series. In July, it pledged more than $1 billion (€980 million ) for French and European cinema over five years in a fresh deal with the country’s main producer groups. It followed a previous accord in which Canal+ invested €480 million in French and European films from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2027. News of the tax hike for Canal+ also follows in the wake of news that the government was also planning a €47M ($53M) cut in public funds for state broadcaster France Télévisions in 2027 . Pre-empting the confirmation of the Canal+ VAT hike, France’s film and TV guilds put out a statement earlier this week. Bannered “Who wants the skin of French film and TV”, it declared that the Canal+ VAT hike combined with the France Télévisions cut flew in the face of promises made by President Emmanuel Macron at his Lumière Summit in September. “That summit…. had the stated aim of placing France at the heart of global creative production,” it read. “France Télévisions and Canal+ are two pillars of French film and audiovisual financing. “Through their investment obligations, pre-buys, and commitments under the media chronology rules, they enable hundreds of projects to get off the ground each year, ranging from debut features and auteur-driven works to genre films and international co-productions. Cutting their resources inevitably reduces their capacity to invest in creative work. Since funding obligations are tied to revenue, every euro taken away from these groups translates into fewer funded projects, fewer shoots, fewer jobs, and less diversity on screen. Targeting both groups in the same budget means striking at the very heart of the French model. title: Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs David Ellison’s “Coziness” With Donald Trump Is “Way Overstated”, Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute; Verizon Responds View All October 2, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc After the expected close of their merger, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will together be known as Skydance . CEO David Ellison revealed the new name Friday in a post on X . The $110 billion merger is projected to be finalized on Tuesday after a year-long pursuit by Ellison and a two-month delay caused by antitrust lawsuits by 12 states and the Writers Guild of America. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” “What once was the peak, is now just the beginning,” Ellison wrote. “Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history – we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.” The choice of the name, he said, stemmed from several objectives. One is to preserve the history of Paramount and Warner Bros. as individual entities under the Skydance umbrella. “We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. – and all our extraordinary brands – to remain in the spotlight.” Watch on Deadline When Skydance acquired Paramount in August 2025, the company wanted to take advantage of Paramount’s familiar consumer brand while also emphasizing Skydance as the corporate parent. That meant the official name was “Paramount, a Skydance Corporation,” which was later streamlined to “Paramount Skydance Corporation.” Before the two large media companies combined, the new entity also faced the legal obstacle of an antitrust lawsuit by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, which labeled it an illegal monopoly. The settlement of the lawsuits, laid out in a 5-year consent decree, requires separation of the Paramount and WBD operations in several business areas. It also tries to guard against one of the major studios being dissolved, as has been the fear of merger opponents. Those precautions meant that a name appearing to favor one merger partner over the other would also be a potential problem. In the absence of any official guidance on the name, colloquial handles like “WarnaMount” or “ParaBros” became commonplace. One stark reality of the new identity is that Discovery Communications, which went public in 2008, two decades after the Discovery Channel lit up as a cable network, will now no longer have its name in lights. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. title: It’s Skydance: David Ellison Brands Combined Paramount-Warner Bros. With His Studio’s Title
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:11am David Ellison David Becker/Getty Images The entertainment business’ newest conglomerate has a name: Skydance . David Ellison on Friday shared on X that once Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery combine, the new corporate brand will take the name of the studio he founded 20 years ago. But while that will be the corporate name, Paramount and Warner Bros. will serve as sub-brands. “Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations,” Ellison wrote. “We wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.” The name answers one of the bigger unanswered questions about the new company, which will firmly be among the biggest in the business, alongside The Walt Disney Co. and Netflix. In the entertainment business, the truth is that the corporate brand doesn’t always matter. It does for Disney, which is synonymous with a certain type of family-friendly content, and it does for Netflix, which is synonymous with streaming, but the industry past and present has been filled with owners that have names like Comcast, Viacom, News Corp., Versant, Capital Cities, etc. Hardly household names for most consumers. For most public companies, a corporate name is just a corporate name, a “house of brands” to hold the consumer-facing ones, even if they may share the name of a film studio. Ellison founded the Skydance film studio in 2006, and used it as a vehicle to acquire Paramount last year, before pivoting to Warner Bros. Discovery shortly after. He also posted a sizzle video featuring footage from some of the film and TV projects of the combined company, ending with a title card that perhaps tees up just how how is thinking about the individual brands that will live within Skydance. David Ellison’s reveal of Skydance as the holding corporation name. @ellisonskydance/X The card features the Skydance logo in the middle, surrounded by the logos for the Paramount and Warners film studios, CBS, HBO Max, Paramount+, DC Comics, Nickelodeon, and CNN, suggesting the importance of those brands to the larger strategy. Reading between the lines, one gets the sense that the film studios and streaming platforms will retain their own identities, with CBS (sports and broadcast), Nickelodeon (kids and family) and CNN (news) anchoring their own parts of the business. “We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks,” Ellison wrote. “At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance.” The $111 billion mega-merger is slated to close next week, with Ellison joined by former Mattel chief Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. title: ‘Night Of The Living Dead’ Vertical Microdrama Readied For Horror-Focused App Room418
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Prime Video’s ‘Bloodaxe’ Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand & Lasse Steen To Cast Disney+ & Indonesia’s Vidio Launch Subscription Bundle ‘Shaka iLembe’: First Look At Season 3 Of MIPCOM-Bound African Zulu King Drama View All October 2, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dylen Postnikoff is a co-founder and CEO of Room418; the original 'Night of the Living Dead' Courtesy/Everett Collection EXCLUSIVE: A newly-established microdrama business geared towards horror is adapting genre classic Night of the Living Dead ahead of its full launch. L.A.-based Room418 is positioning itself as a studio and platform that puts “vertical-first originals at the center of a dedicated destination for horror fans, alongside curated programming in vertical, horizontal and mixed formats.” A slate of acquired shows will launch the vertical video app, with original productions following. Related Stories News Vertical Video Economy Worth $150B, Even Without China – Owl & Co Report News Vertical Video Studio LoveHit Launches With Adaptations Of Literary Classics Starring Microdrama Regulars & Eric Roberts Former Blink49 Studios, CBC and Shaftesbury exec Dylen Postnikoff is leading Room418 as co-founder and CEO. Postnikoff, a comms and marketing specialist who helped shape the international profiles of Schitt’s Creek and Anne With an E , has been working at Wild Cards maker Blink49 since June last year . With horror from emerging creators already one of the stories of the year in film and TV through the successes of Curry Barker’s Obsession and Kane Parsons’ Backrooms , Room418 is looking to tap into the zeitgeist. As such, it is planning on working with creatives who’ve found success on Wattpad and digital platforms. Watch on Deadline An invite-only beta version of the Room418 app will launch this fall ahead of a commercial launch, featuring a slate of licensed horror content. Ten original and adapted projects have been optioned and are in development as well. Notably on the development slate is a vertical reimagining of George A. Romero’s 1968 horror classic Night of the Living Dead . The film has been in the public domain since its original release due to an error by its original distributor. The news comes hours after Deadline revealed filming has wrapped on Twilight of the Dead , a horror pic considered the “final chapter” of the late Romero’s zombie saga. Also on the slate is a screen adaptation of Ben Sobieck’s When the Black-Eyed Children Knock , which was popular on Wattpad. Room418 and Slash Management are also co-producing an original project with digital horror creator Monse Gutierrez, whose social handle is @CVNELA. The company is also collaborating with L.A.-based REELi Studios on an original horror series inspired by Filipino folklore, with production planned in the Philippines. “What makes horror so interesting globally is that fear is universal, but the mythology is local,” said Postnikoff. “Every market has its own stories, folklore and voices, and horror audiences are unusually willing to cross borders to discover them. At the same time, mobile has changed where discovery actually happens. We’re building Room418 to connect a global genre audience with a new generation of creators and stories designed for the way people are watching now.” The Room418 team see horror as particularly well-suited to the growing microdrama market, with cliffhangers and fan culture making aligning the genre with vertical video’s quick-hit format. “Vertical changes more than the frame,” said Postnikoff. “It changes the rhythm of the storytelling, how quickly you establish a world, where you build tension and how you earn the next episode. What excites us is what that unlocks. “A microseries can be a complete entertainment experience in its own right, but it can also introduce a filmmaker, prove an audience for an idea and become the first expression of IP that grows into film, television and beyond.” Postnikoff has worked in entertainment and media for more than 15 years, leading on brand and franchise strategy for the likes of Murdoch Mysteries and Kim’s Convenience . She’s hoping to apply her expertize in studio positioning, corp comms and audience growth to Room418’s mission to create a horror-first destination for genre fans. Room418 is working with technology firm KINO Studios on the app’s product and technical infrastructure. Members of KINO’s founding team previously were executive producers on A24’s Undertone , which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. Should Room418 originals be successful, the company is eyeing expansions into film, television, adaptations and experiences. The invite-only beta of the Room418 app will launch later this fall ahead of the company’s commercial rollout. title: U.S. Job Growth Slowed To 29,000 In September, With Slight Dip In Movie And Music Employment
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories Warner Bros Fires Off Cease And Desist Over Fox Nation’s ‘The Vow,’ But Network Rejects Claim New Series Infringes On ‘The Bachelor’ Fox Business To Debut ‘Big Money In The Morning’ To Replace Maria Bartiromo’s Show View All October 2, 2026 5:46am Add us as a Google Preferred Source U.S. Department of Labor building in Washington, D.C. Robert Knopes/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images U.S. job growth slowed in September to 29,000, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. Overall, the employment situation was largely unchanged during the month, amid continued concerns over rising prices. Employment in movies and music dipped slightly, shedding about 200 jobs to 328,500. Employment among broadcasting and content providers fell by 3,000, to 328,100. Industry lobbyists have pointed to job losses in movie and TV production as they press for passage of a 20% federal incentive, with hopes that Congress will take up a bill during the lame duck session. Watch on Deadline The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised previous months’ figures, as is typical. The figures for July were changed downward by 31,000, showing a loss of 10,000 jobs. August’s job numbers, which were surprisingly robust, were revised down by 29,000 jobs, to 133,000. The biggest gains were in health care, adding 17,000 jobs, while there was a slight growth in construction and manufacturing jobs. The average hourly earnings rose by 5 cents, or 0.1%, to $37.81. Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have risen by 3%. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal, called the report “mediocre.” She wrote on X, “The biggest sore spot = wage growth of 3% in past year. title: ‘Concrete Turned to Sand’ Dives Into Oyster Farms, With Otherworldly Imagery From the ‘Backrooms’ DP (Exclusive Clip)
full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 2, 2026 5:45am 'Concrete Turned to Sand' film still Courtesy of Slag Pile Films If the liminal atmosphere in Backrooms , enhanced by the cinematography of Jeremy Cox, gave you a sense of dread, his camera work on Concrete Turned to Sand will take you into a very different space – oyster farms in British Columbia, Canada. Yes, oyster farms! But again, you better get ready for an immersive sensory cinematic experience that will plunge you into a world full of otherworldly, almost sci-fi-esque, images and all sorts of different emotions and sensations. The film from Vancouver-based directors Jessica Johnson and Ryan Ermacora, will screen, starting on Oct. 11, in the BFI London Film Festival ‘s (LFF) Documentary Competition program, but it is not your regular doc. In fact, notes about the film, which is shot on 35mm, describe it as “a radical refusal of the conventional documentary narrative.” Related Stories Business MIA Market Unveils 2026 Program, Lineup For Digital Era TV Daniel Ezra's Full-Circle Goodbye to 'All American' The movie from Slag Pile Films received its world premiere at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival in Toronto and will now celebrate its international premiere in London. Audiences can expect natural richness, such as underwater images of glistening shellfish, to encounter ecological dread. After all, the oysters on the coast of the Discovery Islands that are featured in the film take years to reach maturity, but all around them, the pace of environmental change is accelerating. And through Cox’s lens, nature looks, and almost feels, otherworldly. The film’s soundscape, created with sound artist and musician Scott Gailey, adds another key sensory layer. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films Don’t expect a multitude of data charts and the like, though. After all, the press notes for the film highlight: “Amid accelerated climate change and lives increasingly hyper-mediated by technology, the film resists the impulse to explain, choosing sensation over exposition.” You can catch a trailer for Concrete Turned to Sand right here, but THR can now also premiere an exclusive clip from the film at the end of this post. Through their work, Johnson and Ermacora explore “the convergence of labor, landscape and the political and economic forces that shape them.” As a result, in Concrete Turned to Sand , oyster farming becomes a lens for the collision of different time scales: the years it takes an oyster to mature, the accelerating pace of environmental change, and the geological time of our planet. And that is by design. After all, the creative team explains: “By placing human labor and science within these vastly different temporalities, the film asks us to reconsider not only how we look at the state of the environment, but how we understand our own brief presence – and effect – within it.” The rich cinematic imagery and sound give new forms to the often complex and invisible realities of climate change. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films “We worked with scientists to provide insight into ocean acidification and its impacts, while offering perspectives on the geological timescale of our ecological circumstances,” say Johnson and Ermacora. “This project explores methods of representing climate change by experimenting with optical and auditory techniques that play with the distanciation between the viewer and the ecological subject of the film. Concrete Turned to Sand creates an encounter between the beauty and strangeness of our world, engaging us to think beyond our atomization and towards broader ecological understanding and context.” For some scientific insight and to get another glimpse into the world of the film, check out an exclusive clip from Concrete Turned to Sand below. title: International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich
full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns With Biggest Ever Launch Ep Of Nearly 9 Million Viewers BBC Gives First Look At ‘The Last Detectives’ Crime Drama From Matthew Barry, Nicola Shindler View All October 2, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paramount-Warner Bros. is set to close Getty Images Welcome, welcome Insiders. Max Goldbart here taking you through a week in which one of the biggest entertainment deals of this century was waved through. Read on. And sign up here . Merger Approved! Getty Images C-suite winners and losers: In the end it all happened quite quickly. Several weeks back it appeared that David Ellison might feel the full force of regulators in the UK and Europe, not to mention dozens of U.S. state AGs. Fast-forward to Wednesday and the $110B Paramount -WBD mega-merger was officially waved through and the new company will officially launch on Tuesday (October 6). Thoughts moved at lightning speed to the C-suite winners and losers, and we didn’t have to wait long for the departure of Cindy Holland, who it is heavily presumed will be replaced by HBO boss Casey Bloys as chief of streaming across both behemoths. In her email to staff, Holland hinted at Ellison “optimizing for HBO stability,” clearly a somewhat barbed nod to her successor. HBO was talking up its Spanish originals at Iberseries in Madrid this week and all eyes will now be on how much Bloys looks to expand the joint operation’s streaming strategy outside of the U.S., with internationals boss Sarah Aubrey expected to remain by his side. Nellie Andreeva’s deep dive can be found here . One name that wasn’t expected to pop up this week was Ynon Kreiz, the Israeli-born former Endemol Group boss who exited Mattel, and was then swiftly named co-CEO of Par-Warner, sharing top-dog duties with Ellison. Kreiz brings weighty international experience to the new entity, and was for a couple hours rumored to be taking up a big international job before being named co-chief. The long-serving Gerhard Zeiler still holds the international keys at Warner with Kevin MacLellan in an equivalent post at Par. Thoughts now turn to the outposts of both of these big beasts, where there is surely much rejigging and “optimizing” to come. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be Layoffs Executives David Ellison's "Coziness" With Donald Trump Is "Way Overstated", Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale AI Chatter @ RTS London Watch on Deadline BBC Studios Generating headlines: Just a day before the merger completed, Reemah Sakaan, the boss of Paramount UK network 5, was facing tricky questions across the pond over political interference from her new overlords, but she batted them away with aplomb. This was at the RTS London Convention, where the great and good of the Brit TV industry gathered for a day jam-packed with news lines. With hundreds being laid off across the BBC and Channel 4, a new content chief set to be imminently announced at the latter, and the mergers at Sky-ITV and Banijay-All3Media taking hold, there was plenty to address. In the end, it was AI that once again generated headlines. Prime Video international boss Kelly Day laid down the gauntlet with a full-throated backing of AI first up, as she said the tech is “not a threat to creativity,” but is “creativity unleashed.” Not to be out-headlined, BBC DG Matt Brittin then raised eyebrows when he out-the-blue admitted he’d been sent a fully AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. “Pretty good,” was his verdict, leading BBC commissioners in the crowd to choke on their morning coffee. The reality is that the tech is here to stay and the peeps in charge clearly want to be realistic about its benefits… Creatives may take a little while to join them. Steven Knight, who is vehemently anti-AI, spoke a few hours after Brittin. However, all the crowd really wanted to know from the Peaky Blinders creator was the identity of the next 007, given that Knight is writing the Amazon MGM movie (Amazon was also sponsoring the RTS event). In the end, the crowd waited and waited, before all they got was a firm “no” to the question of whether writing the movie about the most famous spy on earth is giving him sleepless nights. Knight was neither shaken, nor stirred. All our RTS coverage can be found here . The Insider Interview: Academy Boss Bill Kramer @ Zurich Photo courtesy of Violeta Sofia Our Deadline Studio in Zurich was replete with big stars and industry names over the past week (for Martin Moszkowicz, Romain Bessi and more click here ), so it was difficult to boil the Insider Interview down to one. In the end we opted for a fascinating sit-down with Academy chief Bill Kramer, Mattel Studios’ Robbie Brenner and Sony Pictures Classics’ Michael Barker. The trio, unsurprisingly, wanted to chat about Obsession and Backrooms, the year’s big hits that look set to usher in a wave of YouTube creatives to mainstream film. For Kramer, their breakout success speaks to “the importance of fandom,” no matter where it comes from. >>> Watch the Interview Global Breakout Big Band Story, TF1 The French TV industry has its challenges at present, but Cat’s Eyes stands out. TF1’s series is about to launch Season 2 and is based on a cult 1980s Tokyo-set manga. The first season was a ratings hit airing on Hulu in the U.S. We checked out what the growing international buzz is all about. >>> Read The Breakout The Essentials Anthony Avellano for Deadline/Sarah Dunn/Getty/Stefan Kokovic/Getty 🌶️ Hot One : Nicolas Cage, Michael Sheen, Jordi Mollà, Emilio Sakraya and Adrian Topol are starring in C.L.A.Y. , a psychological cyber-thriller from Simon Afram. 🌶️ Another : Cast has been confirmed for Woody Allen’s next movie including Marton Csokas and Jemima Kirke. 🥇 Team unveiled: Banijay set out its new sales team under Cathy Payne, with Rachel Job nabbing a top job and a number of long-serving execs exiting. 📆 Premiere date: Indian rural horror Kaali Keti will be given a theatrical release on October 23. 🚪 Closing down: True Brit Entertainment, UK seller of The Death of Robin Hood, has filed for bankruptcy . 🏆 Awards latest: The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award. ⛺ Fest latest: Stewart was at Iberseries in Madrid, where co-pros , YA and the Banijay-All3 merger were in the spotlight. ⏱️ To the Tardis: Multiple BBC Studios labels will likely apply to be the next producer of Doctor Who . 🍿 Box office: KPop Demon Hunters 2 is targeting a “very broad theatrical release,” per Ted Sarandos. 🖼️ First look: At the third season of hit African drama series Shaka iLembe before its MIPCOM debut. title: Mark Ruffalo Slams Approved ParaBros Merger: “Bad Deal For This Country”

title: David Ellison Wants CEO Mark Thompson To Remain At CNN After Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery Deal…
full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 9:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Mark Thompson Photo by John Lamparski/Getty Images for Advertising Week New York Paramount CEO David Ellison wants CEO Mark Thompson to remain at CNN after the Warner Bros Discovery deal closes, a move that would settle at least some of the speculation over the future of the network under its incoming new owners. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” Talks between Ellison and Thompson are said to be in their early stages, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Wall Street Journal first reported on Ellison’s plans to retain Thompson, who was tapped to lead the network in 2023 . Since then, he has sought to integrate the linear and digital operations while launching CNN’s All Access subscription and streaming service. Under Thompson, CNN also has continued to aggressively report on the Trump administration, while embarking on a lawsuit against the president after he banned the network and two other outlets from the White House grounds. The network also has defended its reporters in the face of attacks by the president, including its chief White House correspondent, Kaitlan Collins. Watch on Deadline Thompson was president and CEO of the New York Times Company from 2012-20, after serving as director-general of the BBC for eight years.

title: Ynon Kreiz, Newly Minted Co-CEO Of Paramount, To Get Pay Bump After WBD Merger Close, $31.5M…
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 2:27pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Ynon Kreiz, who will be co-CEO of the combined Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Ynon Kreiz , who was tapped Wednesday as Co-CEO of the soon-to-merge Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, will collect a $31.5 million signing bonus and at least $35.1 million a year in total compensation by 2027. In an SEC filing Thursday, Paramount laid out terms of the former Mattel CEO’s 5-year contract and said its board of directors approved the appointment of Kreiz on Sunday. His exit from Mattel was announced Wednesday morning, with Paramount revealing his new post later in the day. After a lengthy legal challenge by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America put it in limbo for two months, the $110 billion merger is slated to close on Tuesday. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Kreiz will receive a signing bonus in the form of restricted stock units [RSUs] worth $31.5 million. Beyond the signing bonus, the filing lays out two sets of figures – one covering the brief pre-merger period and then another reflecting the time after the completion of the deal. The official first day of Kreiz’s employment contract is Monday, October 5, meaning he will have had time to put a few office supplies in desk drawers and visit the commissary before the elevated figures take effect. Kreiz, 61, will be paid an annual base salary of $3.5 million, rising to $5 million the day after the merger closes. His annual bonus targeted at $1.5 million will increase to $4.9 million. He will be eligible for 2.6 million shares of Class B stock along with another stock award of 1.25 million shares. Within 15 days after the merger close, he will be granted RSUs worth up to $5.1 million, prorated based on the part of the first year of employment following the merger close. Starting on October 5, 2027, the first anniversary of the start of the contract, Kreiz will be granted annual equity awards worth $20.1 million. While there are a number of variables, as is always the case with executive compensation, the upshot of the new figures is that Kreiz will be at the high end or above the range of his recent pay at Mattel.
